items.title: test: TestClaudeClientCacheAbsentUnchanged is red wherever /bin/sh's echo leaves \n as written (bash as sh), green on dash
items.body:
Found while running the full suite on Linux (Arch, `/bin/sh -> bash`), on main 87d703c5.

## What is red

```sh
GOTOOLCHAIN=go1.26.8 go test -tags nogui -count=1 -run TestClaudeClientCacheAbsentUnchanged ./internal/gateway/
--- FAIL: TestClaudeClientCacheAbsentUnchanged (0.00s)
    claude_client_cache_test.go:291: ordinary prompt changed: ...
```

Red on every run (5/5 with `-count=5`), on a clean checkout of 87d703c5, with `umask 022`. It is red at e72b6a33 and d9e87eb3 (#1717) too, and at every later commit that touches `internal/gateway/claude_subscription.go` (20c06883, e183604f, f550d369, ec645439).

## Why

The harness script (`newScriptHarness`, internal/gateway/claude_resume_test.go) logs each turn with

```sh
echo "told $line" >> $log
```

The body it is given holds the prompt's newlines JSON-escaped (literal `\n`). The test expects them as **real** newlines in the log:

```go
"...\u003c/external_system_instructions\u003e\n\n"   // real LF, LF
```

so the expectation is only met when the shell's `echo` re-interprets backslash escapes:

- dash (Ubuntu CI's /bin/sh): `echo "a\nb"` prints a real newline — the test passes.
- bash as /bin/sh (Arch; and macOS /bin/sh is bash 3.2 as sh, whose echo also leaves `\n` unless xpg_echo): `echo "a\nb"` prints `a\nb` — the test is red.

```
$ sh -c 'echo "a\nb"' | od -c        # here (bash as sh)
0000000   a   \   n   b   \n
```

So the test's own harness depends on the shell's `echo` escape handling, and any machine without dash as /bin/sh sees the package red.

## Fix direction

Log with `printf 'told %s\n' "$line"` (no escape re-interpretation, same bytes on every shell) and hold the test's expectation to the literal `\n` the body carries — or make the harness unescape deliberately and say so. Any other assertion in the resume tests that spans a newline in a told line is riding the same dash behavior and would need the same pass.

items.title: gateway: SophNet's model-scoped 429 ("Model tpm limit exceeded") rests the whole key, greying out every model on it
items.body:
## Summary

When a SophNet model answers a **model-scoped** 429, magpie rests the **whole API key**, so every sibling model on that key is greyed out on the Routing page (`rate limited · back in 59 s`) and gets a local 429 without the request ever reaching upstream.

This is the same shape as #3039 (a relay's `for model <X>` 429) and #3213 (Qoder's per-model 503), but it arrives with **different wording** that none of the existing matchers catch:

```
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests

{"error":{"message":"SophNet: Model tpm limit exceeded. Please try again later."}}
```

## Evidence from the gateway trace

A group `group/deepseek-v4-flash` with three members on one SophNet key. The first member gets the 429 above, and `/api/gateway/trace` records the rest against the **key**:

```json
{
  "id": "sophnet",
  "model": "DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017",
  "status": 429,
  "fail": "rate",
  "error": "SophNet: Model tpm limit exceeded. Please try again later.",
  "rest": {
    "why": "rate",
    "status": 429,
    "until": "2026-10-25T22:54:24Z",
    "by": "cooldown",
    "failures": 1,
    "key": "sophnet@api key …pncw"      // ← whole key, not restID()
  }
}
```

The next two members were tried within ~1s and each got its own 429, after which all three rows showed `rate limited · back in 59 s`. The same happens for every other model on that key.

## Expected

Recognise `Model <name> limit exceeded` (and similar "the limit is for this model" phrasing) as a **model-scoped** refusal and call `c.restID()` instead of `c.restKey()`, like `otherModels` does for `switch to other models` in #3039.

The distinction matters here: SophNet's console exposes per-model TPM/RPM (e.g. 600k TPM, 120 RPM per model), so a `Model tpm limit exceeded` does not necessarily mean the key's whole quota is gone. If the sibling models are in fact on a shared pool, letting the request go upstream and answer its own 429 is still more truthful than pre-emptively refusing it locally with another model's error text.

## Trade-off worth considering

I understand the conservative choice (don't hammer a key that just 429'd). A middle ground could be: rest the model immediately, but for siblings only apply a short "probe" cooldown (or none), and rest the whole key only if a second distinct model on the same key also 429s.

## Environment

- magpie 0.1.1543, Linux (workstation), custom SophNet plugin provider (`@ai-sdk/openai` / `@ai-sdk/openai-compatible`, per-model `limit.context` / `limit.output`)
- Three channels under one SophNet API key: `DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017`, `-global`, `DeepSeek-Flash-1017`, routed `order`/`auto`
- Reproduced by sending concurrent requests through the group until SophNet answers `Model tpm limit exceeded`

## Workaround

Routing page → `Try now` on the key lifts the rest immediately (as #3039 notes); restarting magpie also clears it.

items.title: [Bug] Routing: live request's Context window card says "the model's window isn't known" while the model's window is known
items.body:
## What happens

On the Routing page (`?view=routing`), the **Context window** card of an in-flight request shows:

```
CONTEXT USED
107K tokens
THE MODEL'S WINDOW ISN'T KNOWN
```

even though the same model's window is known everywhere else — the provider panel on the right of the same page shows `1M`, and `magpie model context sophnet/glm-5.3-flashx` prints `1M`.

This happens for every model and every routing group, as long as the request is still running (the card carries the green **Live** badge). Once the request finishes, the card shows the window correctly.

## Root cause (from the gateway's own data)

`GET /api/gateway/trace` returns `routes[]` where the in-flight entries have no `prompt.window`, while finished entries do:

```
in-flight (done=false):
  group/sonnet-5-5        prompt.window=null  prompt.tokens=410997
  group/deepseek-v4-flash prompt.window=null  prompt.tokens=110233

finished (done=true):
  prompt.window=1000000  prompt.tokens=98913
  prompt.window=1000000  prompt.tokens=99238
```

`context.js` then renders the fallback text:

```js
const window = p.window || 0;
...
} else sub.textContent = t("the model's window isn't known");
```

So the window is only filled in when the trace row is finalized; the live row never carries it, even though the model (or every member of the group) already has a known `limit.context` in the catalog.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Configure a routing group, e.g. `group/deepseek-v4-flash` (three SophNet channels).
2. Send a request through the gateway from any agent (Claude Code is the easiest).
3. Open `?view=routing` while the request is running.
4. Look at the **Context window** card — it says `THE MODEL'S WINDOW ISN'T KNOWN`, while the provider rows on the same page show `1M`.

## Expected

One of:

- the live trace row carries the window of the model (or the largest window among the group's members) as soon as routing decides, or
- if the window genuinely cannot be known yet, the card says something neutral (e.g. omit the sentence, or show `tokens` without the "unknown" claim) instead of asserting the model's window is unknown.

## Environment

- magpie 0.1.1543, Linux (workstation), `magpie web --addr 0.0.0.0:3430 --lan`
- Provider: custom plugin with per-model `limit.context` / `limit.output` (20 models, all of them have `context` set; none is missing)
- Agents affected: Claude Code (`~/.claude/settings.json`), regardless of model or group
- Verified the catalog is complete: `GET /api/providers` returns `context: 1000000` for every model, and `/api/context` reports the correct `window` for finished sessions

items.title: usage: a web search sent to Kimi Code's or WorkBuddy's search service, or to a search API, leaves no row in Usage › Requests
items.body:
neiko (Discord) asked whether magpie's helper requests can reach a provider without the user seeing it. Most can't go unseen: a model search, an image description and a routing classification go through `s.serve`, so each one is a request-log row with Kind `web_search`, `vision` or `routing`. Three web-search paths send their own HTTP request and never write a row:

- Kimi Code's search service: `kimiSearch`, internal/gateway/search_kimi.go:101-125. It does `s.client.Do` directly; `s.metered` only counts RPM (rpm.go:246).
- WorkBuddy's search: `wbSearch`, internal/gateway/search_workbuddy.go (POST to `origin+wbSearchPath`, line ~63).
- The search APIs (Tavily/Brave/…): `apiSearch`, internal/gateway/search_api.go. They run first when Search first = API, last otherwise, or alone when Searcher is off (search.go:667-707).

So a user who asks "what did magpie send to Kimi/my search key" finds nothing in Requests, though each of these spends the plan's or the key's allowance. Found by reading the code at ffe493773; not reproduced with a real account.

Fix direction: write each one as a request-log row under its provider (or the search API's name) with Kind `web_search`, as magpie's model searches are. Whether it counts toward totals the way a model search does needs deciding: it has no tokens, only a call.

items.title: gateway: switching from Vertex Gemini to Antigravity sends a rejected thought signature
items.body:
## What happens

In Magpie 0.1.1367, continuing a conversation after switching from the GCP AI plugin’s Vertex Gemini 4 Argon to the Antigravity `gemini-3.8-flash` provider returns:

```
400 Antigravity: Corrupted thought signature.
```

In the same conversation, switching from Vertex Gemini to GPT succeeds. The failure is reproducible on the Antigravity request path; no real Google model call is needed to understand the missing recovery branch.

## Why this appears to happen

Magpie preserves Gemini signatures in tool-call history and can put them back into Code Assist requests. In `internal/gateway/codeassist.go`, `buildCodeAssistSent` forwards `Part.Signature` as `thoughtSignature` (and does the same for signed text parts).

Magpie already has recovery for a Gemini signature rejected by Vertex AI: `internal/gateway/gateway.go` retries after `vertexSignatureRefused` and `withoutSignatures` in `internal/gateway/vertex.go`. But this retry is gated on `p.IsVertex()` and the matcher only recognizes `Invalid thought signature`. Antigravity is Code Assist, and reports `Corrupted thought signature`, so the existing recovery is skipped and the 400 is returned.

The local usage record for this report showed a successful Vertex Argon request, then Antigravity Flash 400, then a successful GPT request in the same session. The stored signature references for that session’s Argon tool calls were present and passed the sigstore hash check, so this does not look like a missing/corrupted local signature file. It is still possible the target rejects a complete signature because it came from a different backend/model; request-level comparison would establish that conclusively.

This is distinct from #1536: there a client truncates the tool-call ID/signature payload; here the signature references in the local store are intact and the target is Antigravity after a provider switch.

## Suggested fix

Extend the existing one-time signature-rejection recovery to Antigravity Gemini/Code Assist requests and recognize both `Invalid thought signature` and `Corrupted thought signature`. On that specific 400 only, retry a copied request with incompatible historical tool-call signatures removed, using the Code Assist path’s supported unsigned-history behavior. Keep the original request/history intact, retain signatures on normal same-provider continuation, and do not retry other 400s. Please account for signed text parts separately if they can also trigger this error.

## Regression tests

- Antigravity rejects a historical signature with `Corrupted thought signature`: retry once without the incompatible signature and succeed.
- Vertex’s existing `Invalid thought signature` retry remains unchanged.
- A successful same-provider tool-call continuation still carries its signature.
- Other 400 responses do not trigger a signature retry.
- Verify the behavior for tool-call signatures and, if applicable, text-part signatures.

Magpie 0.1.1367 source: `internal/gateway/codeassist.go`, `internal/gateway/gateway.go`, `internal/gateway/vertex.go`.

items.title: bug(routing): Codex compaction can reclassify an unchanged native turn when transcript identity changes
items.body:
## Problem

An ongoing Codex task can be classified again after context compaction even though its native turn ID has not changed and no new task was submitted. This adds a classifier call and can make the route depend on the summary instead of the original task.

Observed on v0.1.1330. In one correlated routing/session trace, the parsed route turn changed from 7 to 1 immediately after compaction; a fresh classification appeared for the same native turn. The chosen model happened to stay the same, so this is evidence of duplicate classification, not proof of a model switch or measured monetary loss. No complete production HTTP payload was retained.

## Relevant implementation

At v0.1.1330 (`e00fbdbbc74f9829027a78769cbeb265d6271fb4`), `internal/gateway/rules.go` keys the turn decision by group, conversation identity and `firstWords(req)`, and determines continuation through `turnIn(req)`. Compaction can replace the first user text and renumber the parsed transcript. The v0.1.1363 source inspected also retains this key structure; that release has not been runtime-tested for this report.

## Minimal synthetic reproduction

Use local classifier/provider stubs and the Responses gateway with a Codex client user-agent:

1. Submit a user task with `client_metadata.thread_id="session-a"` and `turn_id="turn-a"` (or the corresponding supported transport metadata). Expect one classifier call.
2. Submit a replacement compacted transcript with different first user text, keeping the same session and native turn. No new task was issued. The current behavior classifies again; expected behavior is to preserve the active turn's decision.
3. Change the native turn to `turn-b`. This must classify again.
4. Also test a genuine native cross-thread delegation arriving inside the same active native turn: it must still establish a new task, rather than being suppressed by session/turn stickiness.

Steps 1–3 were reproduced through the actual gateway handler with loopback stubs. A negative control removing the proposed native-identity hookup makes the compaction assertion fail; restoring it passes. These are protocol-shaped tests, not byte-for-byte production replay.

## Proposed minimal repair (local prototype, not deployed)

- Where supported native metadata exists, bind classification continuity to group + session + native turn (and installation identity when available), rather than mutable transcript first words/parsed turn count.
- Preserve reclassification for a genuine new delegation within an active native turn. Our middleware already exposes the delegation text for classification; a boundary identity distinguishes a new dispatch from its tool continuations.
- Keep legacy behavior for clients without sufficient native identity; exclude prediction/title/description helpers from this binding.
- Preserve existing expiry, rule applicability and capacity checks. Do not pin a model for an entire session or change effort/provider selection.
- Store bounded identity digests, not raw task text, in the continuity state.

This is a repair proposal, not a claim that the prototype is production-ready. Middleware alone cannot reliably control the native classifier cache. Any upstream implementation should also preserve legitimate steering/new-task boundaries and existing concurrency behavior.

## Validation and limits

Local prototype based on v0.1.1330:

- Targeted native-turn, routing, Jev and middleware tests pass with `-race`; `go vet` and diff whitespace checks pass.
- Tests cover compaction continuation, a new native turn, new delegation within a turn, separate sessions, legacy fallback, and removing temporary middleware routing items before provider forwarding.
- Plain full gateway suite completed on both pristine base and patched source: 401.368s and 404.226s. Both fail the same tests: `TestCodexFittedImagesPastTheBudget` (19/30 images with 10 kept), `TestMarshalRawIsEncodingJSON`, and `FuzzMarshalRaw/seed#7` (U+2028/U+2029 escaping). This is not a full-suite PASS. The image test also has a prior report in #2606.
- Full-package race runs were time-limited and did not complete; targeted race success is not full-package race coverage.
- All validation backends were local stand-ins. No real classifier/model requests or review reruns were made for these tests; no production binary/configuration was replaced.

This report intentionally omits account information, real task text, session IDs, local paths and private logs. Would you prefer a standalone regression test or a minimal patch for review?

items.title: [Bug] 走 Messages API 的 Claude 回复，用量里的推理 token 恒为 0（aUsage 不读 output_tokens_details.thinking_tokens）
items.body:
**English summary:** magpie's usage records how much of a reply was reasoning for Chat (`completion_tokens_details.reasoning_tokens`), Responses and Gemini (`thoughtsTokenCount`) replies, and for the Claude subscription path (`cliUsage.gateway()` reads `output_tokens_details.thinking_tokens`). The Anthropic Messages path doesn't: `aUsage` in `internal/gateway/anthropic.go` has no `output_tokens_details`, so every Claude reply over the Messages API (Anthropic, Copilot, Bedrock, relays) is recorded with reasoning 0, whether it is relayed (`usageSniffer`) or translated (the Anthropic decoder). As a result `reasoning_tokens` is 0 in `magpie usage --csv` for all of that traffic, `DecodeOf` times such a reply as if it had no reasoning, and a Chat/Responses upstream's reasoning count is dropped when its reply is translated for an Anthropic client such as Claude Code (the Chat and Responses encoders do carry it). A reference fix with tests is on mdwsk88/magpie, branch `gateway-anthropic-thinking-tokens` (commit [9feac29c6](https://github.com/mdwsk88/magpie/commit/9feac29c6c5f1bd7e0601dc9c77be0bbfb0f4395)).

## 现象

Claude Code（Claude Desktop 的第三方模式）经 magpie 用 Copilot 的 claude-opus-5.5。Copilot 每个回复的 `message_delta` 都带思考 token 数，例如 2026-10-24 的一次（effort high）：

```
"usage":{"cache_creation_input_tokens":3858,"cache_read_input_tokens":12030,"input_tokens":2,...,"output_tokens":1277,"output_tokens_details":{"thinking_tokens":710}}
```

magpie 记下的这一行：output 1277，reasoning 0。2026-10-23 我们做 A/B 测试时，magpie 记下的 277 个经 Copilot 的 claude-desktop 请求，`magpie usage --csv` 的 `reasoning_tokens` 每一行都是 0；同一批运行里，Claude Code 自己的 result 用量都带思考 token 数。

## 原因

- `internal/gateway/anthropic.go` 的 `aUsage` 只读 input、output、cache 几个字段，没有 `output_tokens_details`，`aUsage.usage()` 也就不会填 `Usage.Reasoning`。
- 透传的回复（`sniff.go` 的 Anthropic 分支）和转译的回复（Anthropic 解码器处理 `message_delta`）都经过它，所以两条路都丢。
- 同一个仓库里，`claude_subscription.go` 的 `cliUsage.gateway()` 读了 `output_tokens_details.thinking_tokens`；Chat、Responses、Gemini 的用量也都填了 `Reasoning`。只有 Messages API 这一处漏了。
- 和 #1578 不是同一个原因：那里是请求被路由到 Chat Completions 才丢了思考统计，这里是 Messages API 本身的用量没读这个字段。
- 反方向同理：`Usage.anthropic()` 不写思考 token，Chat 或 Responses 上游的推理数转给 Claude Code 时被丢掉；`Usage.chat()` 和 Responses 的编码都带着。

## 影响

- 用量页和 CSV 里，所有走 Messages API 的 Claude 请求推理数都是 0（Anthropic 官方 API、Copilot、Bedrock、各种中转）。
- 输出速度：`DecodeOf` 对有推理数的回复，只按回答部分、从第一个文字算起；Claude 回复的推理数是 0，就按整段输出（含思考）、从第一个内容算起，和其他协议的口径不一致。
- Claude Code 接 Chat 或 Responses 上游时，拿不到思考 token 数。

## 修复（参考实现）

mdwsk88/magpie 分支 `gateway-anthropic-thinking-tokens`，commit [9feac29c6](https://github.com/mdwsk88/magpie/commit/9feac29c6c5f1bd7e0601dc9c77be0bbfb0f4395)：

- `aUsage` 加 `OutputTokensDetails{ThinkingTokens}`，`usage()` 把它填进 `Usage.Reasoning`；
- `Usage.anthropic()` 在 `Reasoning > 0` 时写回 `output_tokens_details.thinking_tokens`（为 0 时输出不变）。

新测试：

- `TestAnthropicThinkingTokensCounted`：用上面那次 Copilot 回复的原始字节（签名截短），分别经 `/v1/messages`、`/v1/chat/completions`、`/v1/responses`，检查用量行的 reasoning 是 710，以及客户端拿到的 usage 里有这个数。
- `TestTranslatedReasoningToldAsThinkingTokens`：Chat 上游报 `reasoning_tokens: 100`，Claude Code 客户端的 `message_delta` 里应有 `"output_tokens_details":{"thinking_tokens":100}`。

## 验证

在 upstream b437e4a 上加这次改动（go1.26.9，macOS，临时 HOME，Go 缓存固定在原位置）：

- 两个新测试通过。把 `anthropic.go` 换回原样后两个都失败：三条路径都报 `thinking tokens not counted: 200 output 1277 reasoning 0`；转译的回复报 `message_delta doesn't tell the thinking tokens`。
- 改动的文件 `gofmt -l` 无输出；`go vet ./...` 在 darwin、linux（`-tags nogui`）、windows 上都通过；三个平台 `go build` 都通过。
- `go test -tags nogui -timeout 45m ./...`：69 个包全部通过（internal/gateway 426 秒）。
- 没试：拿改过的版本接真实上游。测试用的是 Copilot 真实回复的字节；Anthropic 官方 API 也返回同一个字段。

## 相关观察（不在这次修复里）

- Copilot 的 `message_delta` 还带 `copilot_usage`：按类型列出 token 数和单价，以及 `total_nano_aiu`（上面那次是 4724400000）。magpie 的 credits 字段现在只给 WorkBuddy 的 `usage.credit` 用；如果想显示 Copilot 的 AI 用量，可以从这里取。
- 顺带确认过、不需要改 magpie 的两件事：
  - Copilot 单次回复超过约 630 秒会被对端断开（`CANCEL; received from peer`），magpie 已经按协议补发 `event: error`（`streamFailure`）。
  - Copilot 不发思考进度（`thinking_delta` 里没有 `estimated_tokens`）。magpie 转发了 `thinking-token-count-2026-05-13` beta，是 Copilot 那边没给。

items.title: [Bug] gateway/Kimi: typed $ref target containing an untyped object oneOf still causes schema rejection
items.body:
## 问题

Magpie 的 Kimi Code 路线能处理 `$ref` 直接指向无类型 `oneOf` 的简单情况，但下面这种**已声明类型的引用目标内部再包含无类型 oneOf**仍返回：

```text
400 Kimi Code (China): tools.function.parameters is not a valid moonshot flavored json schema,
details: <At path 'properties.x': detected infinite recursion without termination condition>
```

最小复现没有引用循环。只给内部 union 补 `type: object`，相同路线返回 200 / OK。

关联：[WorkBuddy 插件 #378 的三路实测补充](https://github.com/magpie-community/plugins/issues/378#issuecomment-6394043743)。本 issue 聚焦 Magpie 自身的 `kimi-code-cn` 网关路径；WorkBuddy/Qoder 插件的整理逻辑由插件仓库处理。

## 最小请求

发送到已配置 Kimi Code 的 Magpie 网关 `POST /v1/chat/completions`：

```json
{
  "model": "kimi-code-cn/k3.1-pro",
  "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "Do not call tools. Reply exactly OK."}],
  "tools": [{
    "type": "function",
    "function": {
      "name": "probe",
      "description": "Diagnostic placeholder.",
      "parameters": {
        "type": "object",
        "properties": {"x": {"$ref": "#/$defs/X"}},
        "$defs": {
          "X": {
            "type": "object",
            "properties": {
              "y": {
                "oneOf": [
                  {"type": "object", "properties": {"mode": {"type": "string", "const": "a"}}},
                  {"type": "object", "properties": {"mode": {"type": "string", "const": "b"}}}
                ]
              }
            },
            "required": ["y"]
          }
        }
      }
    }
  }],
  "max_tokens": 32000,
  "reasoning_effort": "high",
  "stream": false
}
```

唯一改动：给 `tools[0].function.parameters.$defs.X.properties.y` 加 `"type": "object"`。原始请求 400，修改后 200 / OK；将 `X` 内联、移除这次引用，也能成功。

## 实际 dsh 验证

2026-10-25，以 `dsh headless 0.2.1-rc.2` 运行完整 REA 工具集，共 198 个工具，其中 170 个 REA 工具：

- 原始工具集：Kimi Code 返回 400，错误位置 `properties.after_scenario`，dsh 退出码 1。
- 在临时诊断请求中给 object-only 的无类型 oneOf 补类型：200，最终回复 `OK`，dsh 退出码 0，持久化 session 为 `completed`。
- 实际路由已由网关记录确认是 `kimi-code-cn`，返回模型为 `k3.1-pro`。
- 最终规则在这份工具集中命中 55 处，涉及 29 个工具；含仅接受直接 object 分支的 54 处版本时，Kimi Code 已成功。第 55 处是本地引用分支，对 WorkBuddy/Qoder 插件路径也必要。

原始工具定位为 `mcp__rea__compare_web_captures`。`after_scenario` 的引用目标自身已有 object 类型，但其后代 `steps → items → artifacts` 中有未声明类型的 object union。对完整 compare 工具补齐 12 个同类节点后，单工具请求也成功。

## 当前源码线索

检查时 main 为 `1b039a3c7247d0221fb0b8ed8ef89a35ffd8e9d6`：

- [`collectRefTargets`](https://github.com/yetone/magpie/blob/1b039a3c7247d0221fb0b8ed8ef89a35ffd8e9d6/internal/gateway/kimi_schema.go#L289) 按 `$ref` 查找直接目标。
- 直接目标已有 type 时，`untypedForKimi` 将其排除；目标内部未被另一个 `$ref` 单独引用的无类型 union，未由这个动作补类型。

本次测试时 Magpie 安装文件为 0.1.1485，未重启网关，运行中进程的精确版号未单独确认。上述 main 源码是独立只读检查，未把它当成运行中进程的源码证明。实网失败/成功对照发生在同一运行环境。

## 与 #3205 的区别

[#3205](https://github.com/yetone/magpie/issues/3205) 处理 `{format, description, $ref}` 引用链中间节点被错误添加 type 的问题。本复现的 `X` 已明确为 object，没有引用链中间节点，也不需要在 `$ref` 旁增加 type；缺失的是内部 `y.oneOf` 的 type。因此应单独跟踪，但两个修复需要互相保护。

## 建议验收

1. 覆盖“直接引用无类型 union”和“typed 引用目标内部的无类型 union”。
2. 仅在各分支均明确为 object 时补 object 类型；本地引用需检查缺失和循环，不向引用链中间节点插类型。
3. 保留 anyOf、混合类型 union、examples/default 和非 Kimi 路线的既有语义。
4. 最小复现及真实 REA schema 均做回归；正式版本再跑完整 dsh 会话。

测试只修改工作目录内的诊断请求，没有更改现有配置或插件。现有 34 个配置、插件及程序文件校验和保持一致。本次验证工具声明和文本回合，没有实际执行 REA 工具或验证多轮调用。

items.title: Routing context card: an uncounted prompt reads 1.5–1.6x its neighbours, with no anchor to the last counted value
items.body:
# Context window card: an uncounted prompt reads 1.5–1.6x its neighbours, and nothing on the card says how stale the estimate is

## What I see

In the Routing page's context window card, one request of a long Grok session shows **525,109** prompt tokens in a 1,000,000 window. Every request around it — before and after, all successful — shows **320,900–346,000**. It reads as a context blow-up when the session was nowhere near one.

The row is **uncounted**: the agent cancelled it (status 499, `"the agent canceled the request"`), so no vendor usage came back, `prompt.counted` is absent, and `calibrate` returned early. The card correctly labels it *Estimated*. What it cannot tell me is that this estimate is 1.6x every counted value in the same session.

## What I could and could not verify

**Verified.** Across today's log, 87 non-200 requests have a counted neighbour in the same conversation: the median uncounted/counted ratio is **1.50**, and 81 of 87 exceed 1.2. In this session the ratio drifts slowly over the run (1.45 → 1.50 → 1.61 → 1.64) instead of jumping, and it is spread evenly across every part — including the system prompt and the tool definitions, which cannot grow 62% between two requests 18 seconds apart in the same turn:

| part | 18:24:09 (counted, 200) | 18:24:27 (uncounted, 499) | ratio |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| system | 1,209 | 1,961 | 1.622 |
| tools | 6,228 | 10,104 | 1.622 |
| memory | 1,810 | 2,937 | 1.623 |
| files | 94,445 | 153,231 | 1.622 |
| results | 16,409 | 26,712 | 1.628 |
| chat | 203,407 | 330,164 | 1.623 |

**Not verified.** I could not tell whether the body really was 1.6x larger, or whether the estimate drifted. Two things point away from a plain bug and I do not want to claim one:

- The item *counts* are the same in both rows (`run_terminal_command` n=567 vs 568, `search_replace` n=242, 20 chat turns), so this is not double-counting the same items.
- The same 1.6x applies to a single item's tokens (`turn 3`: 65,078 → 105,584), so it is not one part being added twice.

So either that request carried a genuinely duplicated/larger body from the agent, or one of the two sides (a cached read that the agent replayed, a vendor prefix the agent re-sent) is unaccounted for. I did not keep the body; `promptBodies` holds only the last 10 requests, so I cannot answer it after the fact. That is itself the thing I'd like fixed: see below.

**Ruled out.** `imageTokens = 1600` (`prompt.go:94`). I suspected the fixed per-image cost was compounding over a long session — the image item does grow from 1,590 to 139,200 (87 images) across the run. But on today's 87 uncounted rows the correlation between image share and inflation is **-0.21**, and image-free rows inflate *more* (median 1.78) than image-heavy ones (median 1.50). Not the cause.

**Also ruled out.** CJK over-counting. This session is only 0.7% non-ASCII, and `tokensOf` already charges non-ASCII one token per character.

## What would have saved me

I spent a while checking the agent's own counters against magpie's because the card gave me a number with no anchor. Three things would fix that:

1. **Show the anchor.** Beside an *Estimated* number, show the same conversation's last counted prompt (and how many requests ago it was). A 525K estimate next to "last counted: 323K, 2 requests ago" is self-explaining; 525K alone is not.
2. **Say what the estimate is based on.** The card's tooltip says "Estimated from what the agent sent: the vendor didn't say how many tokens it read". The part that matters for a long session is that the estimate is a bytes/4 reading of the request body with no vendor correction — so it carries whatever duplication the agent sent, and no ceiling from the last real value.
3. **Keep the body of an uncounted request a little longer**, or keep its parts, so a report like this one can be answered. Right now a 499's body is gone by the time anyone looks.

A cap — an uncounted estimate shown at no more than, say, the last counted value plus the estimated growth since — would also stop this from reading as an imminent overflow, but that is a judgement call about what the number should mean, and I'd rather leave it to you than prescribe it.

## Record (redacted)

`~/.config/magpie/routing/2026-10-21.jsonl`, same `conv`, consecutive requests:

```json
{"time":"2026-10-21T18:24:09","status":200,"model":"workbuddy/deepseek-v4.1-flash","prompt":{"window":1000000,"tokens":323508,"counted":true,"turns":20,"parts":[{"kind":"system","tokens":1209},{"kind":"tools","tokens":6228},{"kind":"memory","tokens":1810},{"kind":"files","tokens":94445},{"kind":"results","tokens":16409},{"kind":"chat","tokens":203407}]}}
{"time":"2026-10-21T18:24:27","status":499,"error":"the agent canceled the request","model":"workbuddy/deepseek-v4.1-flash","prompt":{"window":1000000,"tokens":525109,"turns":20,"parts":[{"kind":"system","tokens":1961},{"kind":"tools","tokens":10104},{"kind":"memory","tokens":2937},{"kind":"files","tokens":153231},{"kind":"results","tokens":26712},{"kind":"chat","tokens":330164}]}}
{"time":"2026-10-21T18:24:30","status":200,"model":"workbuddy/deepseek-v4.1-flash","prompt":{"window":1000000,"tokens":320927,"counted":true,"turns":21,"parts":[{"kind":"system","tokens":1203},{"kind":"tools","tokens":6198},{"kind":"memory","tokens":1802},{"kind":"files","tokens":93463},{"kind":"results","tokens":15657},{"kind":"chat","tokens":202604}]}}
```

The agent's own report for the same moment (`_meta.totalTokens` from the ACP session log): 323,758 at 18:24:27 and 323,931 at 18:24:42. The vendor's usage on the two successful neighbours matches magpie's `counted` values exactly (323,508 / 320,927), which is why I trust those and not the 525K.

## Environment

- magpie 0.1.1307 (macOS menu bar), source `3c38fe5c99df102a6bb0fb11c621331406b8a3a2`
- Provider `workbuddy` / `deepseek-v4.1-flash`, `effort: max`, window 1,000,000
- Agent: Grok CLI (ACP), ~20 turns, images read through a `read_file` tool
- The same inflation shows earlier the same day on `qoder-cn/dfmodel` in the same session (1.45–1.64x), so it is not provider-specific

items.title: [Bug] Claude Desktop 网关模式开了 Enable tool search 后，Copilot 拒绝 tool-search-tool-2025-10-19（400 unsupported beta header），每个会话第一个请求失败，工具搜索实际没生效
items.body:
**English summary:** With Claude Desktop's gateway mode pointed at magpie and its *Enable tool search* setting on (`toolSearchEnabled`), Claude Code asks tool search by Bedrock's and Vertex's beta name, `tool-search-tool-2025-10-19`, because Desktop runs it with experimental betas off. Copilot's Messages API refuses that name: `400 unsupported beta header(s): tool-search-tool-2025-10-19` on the first request of every Desktop session (and on its `count_tokens` calls). Claude Code then turns tool search off for the session and resends with every tool schema inline, so the setting never takes effect through magpie + Copilot. Copilot serves the same request shape (deferred tools, `tool_reference` results) under Anthropic's own name, `advanced-tool-use-2025-11-20`, which is what Claude Code sends from a terminal. magpie already renames this beta the other way for Bedrock (`bedrockBetas`). A reference fix renames it for Copilot accounts, with a test and real runs against a Copilot Business account: mdwsk88/magpie, branch [`copilot-tool-search-beta`](https://github.com/mdwsk88/magpie/tree/copilot-tool-search-beta), commit [eed4be36f](https://github.com/mdwsk88/magpie/commit/eed4be36f6c789cddce51eb77c1f9d3ccf08cc64).

## 现象

- 环境：magpie v0.1.1346（macOS app），Claude Desktop 第三方网关模式（自带 Claude Code 2.1.308），模型走 Copilot Business 的 claude-opus-5.5 和 claude-sonnet-5.5。
- 2026-10-24 12:16，在 Desktop 的 Developer › Configure Third-Party Inference 里打开 Enable tool search（magpie 写的那份配置里多了 `toolSearchEnabled: true`）。
- 从那以后，每个新开或恢复的会话，第一个请求都失败。routing 日志记的是 `Copilot: unsupported beta header(s): tool-search-tool-2025-10-19`（err_type `invalid_request_body`），当天出现 3 次（12:16、13:15、13:26）。
- Claude Code 收到 400 后不报错，而是关掉这个会话的工具搜索，把所有工具定义内联后重发。以 13:26 那个会话为例：第一个请求 37,411 tokens（其中工具 17,119），重发后 100,290 tokens（工具 71,336），之后每个请求都带着约 10 万 tokens 的工具定义。会话里会出现 "ToolSearch is no longer available" 的提示。
- 所以这个开关经 magpie + Copilot 从来没真正生效过，每个会话还白白多一次失败的请求。

## 原因

- **Claude Code 怎么选 beta 名：** 2.1.308 按实验 beta 是否打开来定。打开时用 Anthropic 自己的名字 `advanced-tool-use-2025-11-20`，关闭时用 Bedrock/Vertex 的名字 `tool-search-tool-2025-10-19`。
- **Desktop 网关模式发的是哪个：** Desktop 用 `CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_EXPERIMENTAL_BETAS=1` 关掉实验 beta。Enable tool search 则通过它传给 CLI 的托管设置 `--managed-settings {"env":{"ENABLE_TOOL_SEARCH":"force"}}` 强制打开（CLI 只在 `CLAUDE_CODE_PROVIDER_MANAGED_BY_HOST=1` 时读这份设置）。所以 Desktop 发的是 `tool-search-tool-2025-10-19`。Desktop 自带的配置说明也写明：网关 provider 只会加这个 beta 值，再加上延迟加载和 `tool_reference`。
- **Copilot 不认这个名字，认另一个：** Copilot 的 `/v1/messages` 和 `count_tokens` 都拒绝 `tool-search-tool-2025-10-19`，接受 `advanced-tool-use-2025-11-20`。终端里的 Claude Code（自定义 base URL，实验 beta 开着）发的正是这个名字，延迟加载和 `tool_reference` 经 magpie + Copilot 都正常（10-24 实测 13 个请求全部 200）。
- **magpie 只改了一个方向：** `internal/gateway/betas.go` 的 `betas()` 只给 Bedrock 改名（`bedrockBetas`：advanced → tool-search），没有反方向。
- **magpie 也学不会这个拒绝：** `refuseBetas` 只认 Bedrock 的 "Unexpected value(s) … for the `anthropic-beta` header"，认不出 Copilot 的 "unsupported beta header(s): …"，所以每个会话都会再撞一次。就算认出来，去掉这个 beta 后延迟加载也用不了，所以该改名，不该丢掉。

## 修复（参考实现）

mdwsk88/magpie 分支 [`copilot-tool-search-beta`](https://github.com/mdwsk88/magpie/tree/copilot-tool-search-beta)，commit [eed4be36f](https://github.com/mdwsk88/magpie/commit/eed4be36f6c789cddce51eb77c1f9d3ccf08cc64)，基于 upstream 7edf5b0：

- `internal/gateway/betas.go` 新增 `copilotBetas`（`tool-search-tool-2025-10-19` → `advanced-tool-use-2025-11-20`）。`betas()` 对 Copilot 账号（`p.Account.Agent == "copilot"`）按它改名，改名放在去重之前，所以两个名字一起给时只发一次。`/v1/messages` 和 `count_tokens` 都走 `forward` → `betas()`，两条都覆盖。只改 Copilot；其他 provider 照 Claude Code 给的名字发，Bedrock 的逻辑不变。
- `docs/subsystems/gateway-routing.md`：在讲延迟加载工具的几条后面加了一条说明。
- 新测试 `TestCopilotToolSearchBeta`：
  - 假的 Copilot Messages API 拒绝 `tool-search-tool-2025-10-19`（错误文本和类型取自 magpie 用量日志里记下的真实拒绝），接受 `advanced-tool-use-2025-11-20`。请求的 beta 列表和形状（`DeferredToolPlaceholder`、延迟的 MCP 工具、`tool_reference`）取自一次真实的 Desktop 网关模式运行。
  - 检查六件事：Copilot 收到改名后的列表，顺序不变，只请求一次；延迟工具和 `tool_reference` 原样到达；终端那个名字原样发出；两个名字无论哪个在前都只发一次；`count_tokens` 也改名，且答案来自 Copilot 而不是 magpie 的估算；不是 Copilot 的 provider 收到原名。

## 验证

在 upstream 7edf5b0 上加这次改动（go1.26.9，macOS，临时 HOME，Go 缓存固定在原位置）：

- **新测试通过。** 故意改坏三种方式，每种都会失败：
  - 去掉改名（即旧代码）：`Desktop's tool search on Copilot: status 400: {"error":{"message":"Copilot: unsupported beta header(s): tool-search-tool-2025-10-19",...}}`。单独测 `count_tokens` 也是同样的 400。
  - 改名对所有 provider 生效：`relay was asked [...advanced-tool-use-2025-11-20...], want ...tool-search-tool-2025-10-19...`。
  - 改名放到去重之后：`Copilot was asked "advanced-tool-use-2025-11-20,advanced-tool-use-2025-11-20"`。
- **构建和全量测试：** 改动的文件 `gofmt -l` 无输出；`go vet ./...` 在 darwin、linux（`-tags nogui`）、windows 上都通过；三个平台的 `go build` 都通过。`go test -tags nogui -timeout 45m ./...`：70 个包里 69 个通过（internal/gateway 451 秒）。唯一失败的是 internal/update 的 `TestRelaunchOpenTriedAgain`（`TempDir RemoveAll cleanup: unlinkat …/003: directory not empty`），和这次改动无关：它在 upstream 7edf5b0 和这个分支上单独各跑 20 次都通过，internal/update 整包在这个分支上 `-count=3` 也通过。从代码看，测试一看到假 `open` 写了 "opened" 就返回，而分离出去的 relaunch shell 还会往那个 TempDir 里的日志追加一条 "open try" 记录（`relaunchScript` 的 `note`），全量测试负载高时会和清理撞上。这个还没单独报。
- **真实验证：** macOS，Copilot Business。临时 HOME 里只放一份 Copilot 登录的副本，`security` 命令换成永远返回"找不到"的替身，所以没有读写真钥匙串，也没有碰正在运行的 magpie 和它的配置。请求方是 Desktop 自带的 Claude Code 2.1.308，带一个 stdio MCP 测试工具，要求模型调用它。

  | magpie | 请求形态 | 结果 |
  | --- | --- | --- |
  | upstream 7edf5b0 | Desktop 网关模式（`CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_EXPERIMENTAL_BETAS=1`、`CLAUDE_CODE_PROVIDER_MANAGED_BY_HOST=1`、`--managed-settings {"env":{"ENABLE_TOOL_SEARCH":"force"}}`），Sonnet 5.5 | 第一个请求 400 `Copilot: unsupported beta header(s): tool-search-tool-2025-10-19`；Claude Code 关掉工具搜索，32 个工具内联重发，请求从 90 KB 变成 149 KB |
  | 修复后 | 同上，Sonnet 5.5；另跑一次 Opus 5.5 [1m] | 全部 200：ToolSearch `select:mcp__probe__echo_probe` → 下一个请求带着 `tool_reference` → 调用延迟加载的 MCP 工具，结果正确；请求一直在约 90 KB |
  | 修复后 | 终端形态（`ENABLE_TOOL_SEARCH=true`，发 `advanced-tool-use-2025-11-20` 和其他实验 beta） | 全部 200，同样走通 ToolSearch → `tool_reference` → 调用 |
  | upstream 7edf5b0 / 修复后 | 直接请求 `count_tokens`：Desktop 的 beta 列表加一个延迟工具 | 修复前 400（同一句报错）；修复后 200，`{"input_tokens":77}`，是 Copilot 自己算的数 |

- **没试：** GHE（`*.ghe.com`）上的 Copilot 账号（同一个 `Agent == "copilot"` 分支，没有真账号可试）；修复后的版本接真实 Desktop app（实测用的是同一个 CLI 二进制，参数和环境变量与 Desktop 启动时一致）。

## 用户侧的临时办法

在修复发布前，Enable tool search 配 Copilot 不会生效，每个会话还多一次失败的请求，可以先关掉（同一个菜单，重启 Desktop 后生效）。关掉后上下文用量和现在一样，因为现在本来就在退回全量工具。

## 相关

- #2971 说的是终端里的 Claude Code 对非官方 `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` 默认关闭工具搜索，开关是 `ENABLE_TOOL_SEARCH`；这里是 Desktop 网关模式，开关是 Desktop 的 `toolSearchEnabled`，问题出在 beta 的名字上。
- 没改：`refuseBetas` 认不出 Copilot 的拒绝措辞（`unsupported beta header(s): x`），所以 Copilot 拒绝的其他 beta 也不会被记住和去掉，每次都会失败。这次的 beta 不能靠去掉解决，所以没放进这个修复；需要的话可以另开一个。

items.title: [opencode-zen-free] free flash models return finish_reason=tool_calls with an empty tool_calls array; tooling clients stall (GLM-5.3-flash-free, DeepSeek-V4.1-flash-free)
items.body:
## Versions

- Magpie app: `0.1.1559` at time of the occurrences (occurrences spanned several same-day auto-updates on 2026-10-26). Latest at filing: `v0.1.1564` (2026-10-26) — **not yet confirmed whether this is fixed in 1562–1564**.
- Plugin: `@magpie-community/opencode-zen-free-auth@0.1.15` (latest as of 2026-10-25).

## Environment

- Provider: `opencode-zen-free` (OpenCode Zen free tier, `https://opencode.ai/inference/v1`), keyless (`public`).
- Models: `opencode-zen-free/glm-5.3-flash-free:max`, `opencode-zen-free/deepseek-v4.1-flash-free:max`.
- Client: Hermes Agent — OpenAI Chat Completions surface, streaming, loopback gateway `127.0.0.1:3425`, served through a Magpie weight-routing group.
- Context at failure: ~73K–131K prompt tokens (both models are catalogued with a 200K context, so this is within the window, not an overflow).

## Symptom

The client intermittently receives an assistant turn whose `finish_reason` is `tool_calls` but whose `tool_calls` array is empty and whose content is not usable. Hermes log line (verbatim):

```
finish_reason=tool_calls with empty tool_calls array (narration only) — re-prompting to emit the call (retry 1/3, model=group/hermes-route provider=custom)
```

Hermes must drop the turn and re-prompt. 11 occurrences in one session on 2026-10-26; zero on any other day. No data loss (the retry succeeds).

## Two observed sub-shapes (from the per-request log at `~/.config/magpie/routing/<date>.jsonl`)

### 1. Billed-but-empty (5 of 11)

`status: 200`, `out` = 42–160 completion tokens were billed, the reply arrived as a single chunk (`flow: 1`), with **no** `firstText` and **no** `firstReasoning` — i.e. the model produced output tokens but delivered nothing as text, reasoning, or a usable `tool_calls`. Same shape as #3327 ("the model wrote a tool call that the parser could not turn into one, so it dropped it; Magpie relays it as a finished turn"). Verbatim rows:

```json
{"time":"2026-10-26T10:00:07.190+08:00","model":"group/hermes-route","served":"glm-5.3-flash-free","provider":"opencode-zen-free","status":200,"out":56,"flow":1,"ttft":4902,"usage":[{"provider":"opencode-zen-free","model":"glm-5.3-flash-free","in":73910,"out":56}],"rule":{"n":0,"turn":10,"tokens":77293,"effort":"xhigh"}}
{"time":"2026-10-26T10:04:44.383+08:00","model":"group/hermes-route","served":"glm-5.3-flash-free","provider":"opencode-zen-free","status":200,"out":42,"flow":1,"ttft":2453,"usage":[{"provider":"opencode-zen-free","model":"glm-5.3-flash-free","in":1807,"out":42,"cache_read":73984}],"rule":{"n":0,"turn":12,"tokens":79209,"effort":"xhigh"}}
{"time":"2026-10-26T10:22:42.616+08:00","model":"group/hermes-route","served":"deepseek-v4.1-flash-free","provider":"opencode-zen-free","status":200,"out":160,"flow":1,"ttft":1948,"usage":[{"provider":"opencode-zen-free","model":"deepseek-v4.1-flash-free","in":164,"out":160,"cache_read":73472}],"rule":{"n":0,"turn":11,"tokens":73148,"effort":"xhigh"}}
{"time":"2026-10-26T11:47:15.442+08:00","model":"group/hermes-route","served":"glm-5.3-flash-free","provider":"opencode-zen-free","status":200,"out":96,"flow":1,"ttft":3796,"usage":[{"provider":"opencode-zen-free","model":"glm-5.3-flash-free","in":2851,"out":96,"cache_read":101184}],"rule":{"n":0,"turn":14,"tokens":106731,"effort":"xhigh"}}
{"time":"2026-10-26T11:53:31.215+08:00","model":"group/hermes-route","served":"glm-5.3-flash-free","provider":"opencode-zen-free","status":200,"out":86,"flow":1,"ttft":3731,"usage":[{"provider":"opencode-zen-free","model":"glm-5.3-flash-free","in":1024,"out":86,"cache_read":125120}],"rule":{"n":0,"turn":16,"tokens":130910,"effort":"xhigh"}}
```

### 2. Narration + phantom finish flag (6 of 11)

Text/reasoning streams normally for 2–7s, yet the turn still ends with `finish_reason=tool_calls` and an empty `tool_calls` array — the model narrates an intended call but sets the flag without a payload. Matches #636 ("never emit finish_reason=tool_calls without delivering the corresponding calls").

## Repro attempt (negative) — the relay path is not systematically broken

Through the gateway, 12 clean non-streaming requests to both models with a forced tool call, at ~3K and ~60K context: **12/12** returned well-formed structured `tool_calls` with correct `id` (e.g. glm `62d6f350-…`, deepseek `call_00_…`). So the failures are intermittent and task-state-dependent (complex multi-turn sessions), not a consistent drop.

## What this is not

- Not a Hermes/client bug: the client detects the empty array and re-prompts correctly.
- Not a systematic gateway drop: proven by the 12/12 control probe above.

## Request

`emptyFails` / empty-turn retry is (per #3327) limited to Gemini and Code Assist. Extend it to Chat-surface free models — at minimum `opencode-zen-free/glm-5.3-flash-free` and `opencode-zen-free/deepseek-v4.1-flash-free` — so a reply with `finish_reason=tool_calls` and an empty array (or `out>0` with no content/tool_calls delivered) is retried / failed over instead of being relayed to the agent as a finished turn. Separately, when the `tool_calls` array is empty the `finish_reason` should be reported as `stop`, so a tooling client isn't misled into discarding a turn that actually just has narration.

## Related

- #3327 (GLM-5.3-flash tool turns end empty and are relayed as finished)
- #636 (`finish_reason=tool_calls` reported with no calls delivered)
- #2611 (empty-`id` streamed tool calls relayed as-is — related empty-tool-call relay class)

items.title: [Bug] write_stdin 等待长任务被 tool-loop guard 误判，提前结束 Codex 当前轮次
items.body:
### 问题

在 **Magpie v0.1.1542 / Windows / Codex Desktop** 中，开启默认的 **Stop looping replies** 后，Codex 使用 `write_stdin` 等待一个长时间没有终端输出的命令，连续 8 次得到“进程仍在运行”的结果，Magpie 就会拦截下一次请求，并提前结束当前轮次。

提示包含：

> magpie stopped this turn before it reached the model

现场的子进程在拦截后继续运行，随后实际产出了结果。因此，终端暂时没有新输出，不能直接等同于工具调用陷入死循环。用户需要再次发消息才能让 Codex 继续处理结果。

### 最小复现

以下命令、句柄和返回值均为合成示例，不含真实会话或项目数据。

1. 用 `exec_command` 启动一个超过 4 分钟没有输出的任务，例如：

   ```json
   {
     "cmd": "python -c \"import time; time.sleep(360); print('done')\"",
     "yield_time_ms": 1000
   }
   ```

2. 对上一步实际返回的进程句柄，连续执行 8 次空输入 `write_stdin`。下面以合成句柄 `4242` 为例：

   ```json
   {
     "session_id": 4242,
     "chars": "",
     "yield_time_ms": 30000,
     "max_output_tokens": 10000
   }
   ```

3. 8 次结果都表示任务仍在运行，只有 Chunk ID 和少量耗时变化：

   ```text
   Chunk ID: abc001
   Wall time: 30.0012 seconds
   Process running with session ID 4242
   Original token count: 0
   Output:
   ```

**实际行为：** 下一次模型请求被 Magpie 本地拦截，提示相同工具调用已连续执行 8 次、模型卡住。子进程本身不一定被终止。

**预期行为：** 将运行中进程的等待与重复执行相同工作区分。若需要限制长期等待，应按单独的超时或无进展策略处理，而不是仅凭 8 次相同等待结果就宣告模型死循环。

也可以使用下面的确定性用例复现判定问题。它直接调用原有 `toolLoopOf`，不连接模型、不启动子进程、不真正等待，也不需要任何账号。将代码保存到源码仓库的 `internal/gateway/pending_write_stdin_test.go` 后运行：

```sh
go test -tags nogui ./internal/gateway -run '^TestPendingWriteStdinLoopGuard$' -count=1 -v
```

<details>
<summary>确定性回归用例，含重复读文件的对照</summary>

```go
package gateway

import (
	"encoding/json"
	"fmt"
	"testing"
)

// TestPendingWriteStdinLoopGuard distinguishes a pending wait from repeated work.
// All handles and outputs are synthetic; no model, process, or network is used.
func TestPendingWriteStdinLoopGuard(t *testing.T) {
	for _, tc := range []struct {
		name string
		tool string
		args string
		text string
		stop bool
	}{
		{
			name: "pending_wait_must_continue",
			tool: "write_stdin",
			args: `{"chars":"","max_output_tokens":10000,"session_id":4242,"yield_time_ms":30000}`,
			text: "Process running with session ID 4242\nOriginal token count: 0\nOutput:\n",
			stop: false,
		},
		{
			name: "repeated_read_must_still_stop",
			tool: "exec_command",
			args: `{"cmd":"cat example.txt"}`,
			text: "Process exited with code 0\nOriginal token count: 1\nOutput:\nunchanged\n",
			stop: true,
		},
	} {
		t.Run(tc.name, func(t *testing.T) {
			// Eight exchanges use unique call IDs and normal execution metadata.
			var msgs []Message
			for i := range 8 {
				id := fmt.Sprintf("synthetic_call_%d", i)
				result := fmt.Sprintf("Chunk ID: %06x\nWall time: 30.%04d seconds\n%s", i+1, i, tc.text)
				msgs = append(msgs,
					Message{Role: "assistant", Parts: []Part{{
						Kind: ToolCall, ID: id, Name: tc.tool, Args: json.RawMessage(tc.args),
					}}},
					Message{Role: "user", Parts: []Part{{
						Kind: ToolResult, CallID: id, Text: result,
					}}},
				)
			}
			if _, stopped := toolLoopOf(msgs); stopped != tc.stop {
				t.Fatalf("stopped=%t, want %t for %s", stopped, tc.stop, tc.tool)
			}
		})
	}
}
```

</details>

在官方 `v0.1.1542` 上实际运行的关键结果：

```text
--- FAIL: TestPendingWriteStdinLoopGuard/pending_wait_must_continue
    stopped=true, want false for write_stdin
--- PASS: TestPendingWriteStdinLoopGuard/repeated_read_must_still_stop
```

### 分析

相关逻辑在 [`internal/gateway/tool_loop.go`](https://github.com/yetone/magpie/blob/v0.1.1542/internal/gateway/tool_loop.go)：

- `toolLoopRepeats` 固定为 8，`toolLoopOf` 比较末尾连续工具交互。
- `steadyResult` 会归一化耗时与 Chunk ID。这样做对识别重复工作有用，但也使“同一进程仍在运行、没有新输出”的等待结果变得完全一致。
- 当前逻辑没有把 `write_stdin` 的空输入、匹配的运行中句柄及 pending 状态识别为等待。

这不需要某个特定模型才能触发。上述回归用例完全不调用模型；[`serveAgent`](https://github.com/yetone/magpie/blob/v0.1.1542/internal/gateway/middleware.go) 在进入上游路由前就执行 `stoppedToolLoop`，[Codex 自身登录的转发路径](https://github.com/yetone/magpie/blob/v0.1.1542/internal/gateway/codex_backend.go)也执行此检查。模型选择怎样轮询会影响触发概率，但不能据此把这次误判归因于某个模型。这里没有声称已经逐个测试所有模型或协议。

### 建议处理

1. 在构造或比较工具交互时，区分“等待已有任务”和“重新执行同样的工作”。针对本例，只在 `write_stdin` 输入为空、返回值明确包含与参数匹配的运行中句柄时，将其识别为 pending wait，避免计入普通重复工作阈值。若可获得结构化执行状态，优先使用结构化状态。
2. 不要仅按工具名称整体豁免 `write_stdin`。非空输入、句柄无效、重复报错或任务已结束等情况，仍应保留正常判定；等待结果本身也不证明任务健康，长期等待可有独立策略。
3. 保留对重复读取相同文件等真实无效循环的保护，并补充“正常等待不拦截、重复工作仍拦截”的回归覆盖。上面的用例可作为起点。

关闭 **Settings → Models → Replies → Stop looping replies** 可以绕过这个检查，但同时会关闭其他防循环保护，希望正常等待不必依赖全局关闭。

### 验证范围

已核对本机实际运行版本与官方 `v0.1.1542` 源码，并在该版本上运行上述原判定函数的回归用例。撰写时也对比了上游 HEAD 的 `tool_loop.go` 与 `middleware.go`，相关文件无差异；回归用例只在该发布标签上执行。尚未实现或验证修复。原始截图、业务日志、配置、账号、路径和会话标识均不附带。

items.title: gateway/antigravity: a reply restarted inside one Code Assist SSE stream reaches the agent spliced (gemini-4-argon, since 2026-10-21)
items.body:
## Summary

Since 2026-10-21T22:21Z, some `gemini-4-argon` replies served through the Antigravity provider (Code Assist upstream) reach the agent as **one** chat completion whose text is two to four differently worded partial answers glued end to end. magpie's own ledger shows one try and one upstream request for every such reply, so the restarts happen **inside one upstream SSE response**; the Code Assist decoder passes each generation's text parts through as deltas and only reads `responseId` on the first chunk, so nothing tells the client that the reply started over.

Observed on 0.1.1267. In 0.1.1293 (`b641868`) `internal/gateway/codeassist.go` is byte-identical and `continuation.go` differs only in usage accounting, so the behaviour should be the same.

## Setup

- macOS arm64, magpie 0.1.1267 (desktop app), Antigravity provider with one Google AI Ultra account
- model `antigravity/gemini-4-argon`, `reasoning_effort: high`
- client: Pi 1.3.0 (`openai-completions`, `stream: true`) on `/v1/chat/completions`, i.e. `/v1/chat/completions → /v1internal:streamGenerateContent?alt=sse`
- 11 cases from 4 agents between 2026-10-21T22:36Z and 2026-10-22T07:45Z; prompts from 10k to 636k tokens (mostly cached), so it is not tied to context length

## Symptom (shortest case)

One completion, 224 characters, `finish_reason: stop`, 42.7 s, 111 output tokens. Byte offsets of the four segments:

```
@0    在（provider: `kota-local`，model: `magpie/antigr
@46   在！本金刚当前 provider 为 `kota-local`，模型为 `magpie/antigravity/
@102  在（provider：`kota-local`，模型：`magpie/antigravity/gemini
@155  在（provider: `kota-local`，model: `magpie/antigravity/gemini-4-argon`）。
```

Each segment is a fresh generation of the same answer, cut at a different point; only the last one is complete. The larger cases are 5k–19k characters with 2–4 segments. In two of them every segment begins with `Thinking Process:` written as plain text (those rows count 0 reasoning tokens, i.e. the upstream returned no `thought` parts at all for that reply).

## Why it is one upstream response

For the case above, `usage.jsonl` has one row: `in 2049, out 111, ms 42663, ttft_ms 16654, first_text_ms 16654, flow_ms 23816, status 200`, and the matching `routing/<date>.jsonl` record has `tries: 1` with `net.asks: 1`. `nettrace.go` counts every `GetConn` of the try, including a request asked again in place (TryNet: "Asks counts them all, the last one too"), and the try's context is the one `streamTranslated` → `forwardTranslated` use, so any re-ask by the continuation, the empty-reply or the loop path would show `asks ≥ 2`. All nine visibly spliced replies have `tries 1 / asks 1`, and the client saw one HTTP response with one `chatcmpl-…` id.

So the generations were restarted upstream within the single SSE stream, and magpie forwarded each one's text.

## Fingerprint in the ledger

- `in` (promptTokenCount − cachedContentTokenCount) is **exactly 2049** on every such row: the restarted generation hits the implicit cache of the prompt that was just sent. `out` is the sum over all segments (111 tokens for the 224-character example above), and `flow_ms/out` is 18–326 ms/token against ≤ 15 ms/token for normal replies of the same model.
- 15 antigravity rows carry this fingerprint, all `gemini-4-argon`, all between 2026-10-21T22:21Z and 2026-10-22T07:44Z; 0 of the 770 antigravity rows of the 12 days before. Nine of the 15 are visibly spliced; the rest are tool-call-only replies where it cannot be seen in the text. In that window roughly a third to a half of the model's text replies were affected.

## Code reading (`b641868`, same lines in `a15e576`)

- `continuation.go:205` `prefillHow` returns `""` for Code Assist, so `continuation.possible()` is false and a cut stream ends with `errEndedShort` (`:561`, `:649`). That path works as intended — one unrelated reply in the same window ended with `Antigravity: the reply ended before it was complete` and was **not** spliced.
- The empty-reply re-ask and the loop re-ask only fire before anything was said; `holdWriter.mayAskAgain` requires that nothing reached the agent; `textCallSee` only holds text from a `<tool_call>` / DSML mark. None of them applies once text has been sent.
- `codeassist.go:838` `decode` → `:877` iterates candidates and parts → `:910` `d.text()` emits `KText` at once. `:875` reads `ResponseID` only on the first chunk (`geminiChunk` carries it, `:1199`). A later chunk with a different `responseId`, a `usageMetadata.candidatesTokenCount` lower than the one before, or parts arriving after a `finishReason` are not noticed.

## Suggested handling

In `codeAssistDecoder.decode`, remember the first chunk's `responseId` (and the last `candidatesTokenCount`); when a later chunk shows a different `responseId`, a lower count, or content after the stop, treat the reply as restarted:

- if nothing has been said yet, drop what came and go on, as the empty-reply path does;
- otherwise stop reading and end the reply with an error in the client's protocol, as `errEndedShort` does, so the agent asks again instead of showing two answers glued together. A wording agents classify as retryable would let them recover on their own (Pi retries on `service unavailable` / `overloaded` / 5xx, not on "ended before it was complete").

Marking such rows in `usage.jsonl` would also help users find affected turns.

I could not get the raw upstream bodies for these calls (Recent calls had rotated by the time I looked). If it helps I can capture one from the next occurrence, and I am happy to test a build.

items.title: [Bug] ZCode Start Plan 模型过期后仍参与路由，导致订阅模型一并被暂停
items.body:
## 问题描述

ZCode Start Plan 的试用模型过期后，供应商页面已经将它们隐藏，但路由中仍保留这些模型，仅显示为划线状态。实际请求仍会被路由到已过期的试用模型，随后报额度用尽，并触发整个 ZCode 账户的暂停，导致同一账户下仍有效的 GLM Coding Max 订阅模型也无法被路由到。

## 环境

- Magpie 版本：0.1.1560
- 平台：macOS（Apple Silicon）
- 供应商：ZCode / GLM Coding Max
- 已过期的 Start Plan 模型：`GLM-5.3-Flash-Trial`、`GLM-5.3-Trial`
- 受影响的订阅模型：`GLM-5.3-Flash`、`GLM-5.3`

## 复现步骤

1. 在路由分组中加入 ZCode Start Plan 的 `GLM-5.3-Flash-Trial` 和 `GLM-5.3-Trial`，并配置同一账户的订阅模型。
2. Start Plan 试用到期后，供应商页面不再显示这两个试用模型。
3. 打开路由页面，这两个模型仍保留在分组内，显示为划线状态。
4. 继续通过该路由分组发起请求。

## 实际行为与证据

- 供应商当前仅提供 `GLM-5.3` 和 `GLM-5.3-Flash`，但已保存的路由成员仍包含两个过期试用模型，且实际会尝试请求它们。
- 路由日志中的两个试用模型均返回 HTTP 400：

  ```text
  ZCode has no active limited quota for GLM-5.3-Flash-Trial
  ZCode has no active limited quota for GLM-5.3-Trial
  ```

- 随后同一账户下的 ZCode 模型被以共享键 `zcode@zcode` 一并置于暂停状态，包括仍有效的 `GLM-5.3-Flash` 和 `GLM-5.3` 订阅模型。
- 用户截图中，两个试用模型的路由行均显示为划线状态，右侧显示"额度用尽 · 8 分钟后恢复"。
- 界面对当前无供应商提供的成员提示会跳过，但实际路由行为与该提示不一致。

## 期望行为

1. 已过期、已从供应商可用模型列表移除的 Start Plan 模型，应自动从有效路由候选中移除或在请求前跳过，避免继续发起必然失败的请求。
2. 试用到期或特定模型无有效额度，应仅影响对应试用模型；不应因此暂停同一 ZCode 账户下仍有效的订阅模型。
3. 供应商列表、路由界面与实际路由逻辑应保持一致，让可用的 ZCode 订阅模型能够继续正常参与路由。

请修复过期试用模型仍参与路由，以及其额度错误连带阻断订阅模型的问题。

items.title: gateway: with TLS on, a handover still cuts a local connection whose first byte hasn't come yet
items.body:
修 #3568 时顺手看到的。开了 TLS 的 gateway 交接时，本机来的、还没发第一个字节的连接会被直接切掉。现在要桌面端带着 `MAGPIE_TLS_CERT` / `MAGPIE_TLS_KEY` 启动才会碰到，#3085 做完就是设置里的一个开关了。

tlsListener 对本机的连接，先在它自己的 goroutine 里等第一个字节（sniff，最多 10s），读到了才交给 http.Server。listener 一关 `done` 就关了，还在等的连接请求一到，就走进 `hand()` 里 `<-l.done` 那一支被 `c.Close()`（tls.go:288-293），旧 magpie 一个字都没回。http.Server 根本没见过这个连接，所以 #3568 的补丁里"Shutdown 前等每个接下的连接读完第一个请求"那一步也管不到它。

复现：在 #3568 补丁分支的 TestHandedOffGatewayAnswersAConnectionItTook 里，`handOffSandbox` 之前先 `tlsFiles` + `writeCert` 把 TLS 打开（实验用的测试，没提交）。交接和 make dev 两种都是 5/5 红：

```
zz_tls_sibling_test.go:71: a plain request from this computer on a connection the TLS listener took, sent once the end began: "" read tcp 127.0.0.1:...->127.0.0.1:...: read: connection reset by peer (old one answered 1)
```

origin/main 9fc382e6 上也是 5/5 红，那边是 Shutdown 时关的 listener。补丁把关的时机挪到了 HandOff，在 gui/handover.go 的 run() 里两者只隔一行，所以不是补丁带出来的，补丁也没管它。

想到的修法：给 tlsListener 一个只关内层 listener 的 stop，已经接下的 sniff 照样交给 Accept，全交完（或者 sniffWait 到点）Accept 再返回错误。HandOff 和 make dev 的收尾用它，Shutdown 还是原来的 Close。还没动手。

items.title: [feat] agents: draw LobeHub's calls as LobeHub, with its logo (branch ready; PR from fork refused)
items.body:
> **PR creation from a fork is refused** for this account — `gh pr create` answers `hardy-one does not have the correct permissions to execute CreatePullRequest`, the same limit reported in #2792, #2898 and #3582. So it comes as this issue, branch ready to pull or cherry-pick:
>
> **`hardy-one/magpie@agents/lobehub`** — https://github.com/hardy-one/magpie/tree/agents/lobehub (commit `bc2769b`, one commit on `15f0d4c`)
>
> Happy to rework anything below.

## The problem

A LobeHub user who points one of its providers at the gateway sees their calls on the Routing and Usage pages as an unnamed client with a placeholder icon. There is no name to fix, no logo, and nothing on the page says the calls came from LobeHub:

```
   [square icon]
   ● k
   group/deepseek-v4...
```

The `k` is not a LobeHub name. LobeHub sent no `User-Agent` of its own, so its OpenAI-compatible path used the `openai` Node SDK's default, `` `${this.constructor.name}/JS ${VERSION}` ``; a production build minifies the class name to a single letter, so calls arrived as `k/JS 6.49.0` and `AgentOf` read the first word. Any minified build of that SDK would land on the same kind of one-letter name, so it cannot be matched on.

## What changed on LobeHub's side

LobeHub now sends `lobehub/2.2.20` from both layers it talks to a vendor with. Measured against a capture server, not read off the code:

| Request | before | after |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `GET /v1/models` | `k/JS 6.49.0` | `lobehub/2.2.20` |
| `POST /v1/chat/completions` | `k/JS 6.49.0` | `lobehub/2.2.20` |
| `POST /v1/responses` | `k/JS 6.49.0` | `lobehub/2.2.20` |

With that, `AgentOf` already reads `lobehub`, so on a current LobeHub the page shows `lobehub` instead of `k`. What is still missing is the entry magpie keeps, so the name renders as `LobeHub` and the logo is drawn.

A user on an older LobeHub keeps sending the SDK's one-letter name; nothing here can name those, and this change does not try to.

## The change

`internal/agent/agents.go`, in `others` beside `curl` and `pi-desktop`:

```go
// LobeHub reaches the gateway as a provider it was pointed at, with no
// config magpie sets up. Its User-Agent names it, `lobehub/<version>`;
// drawn with its logo on the Routing and Usage pages.
{ID: "lobehub", Name: "LobeHub", Icon: "lobehub-color", UA: []string{"lobehub"}},
```

A client rather than an agent, the shape `docs/integrating.md` describes for an app that keeps its own provider list: LobeHub stores its providers itself and there is nothing for magpie to write or restore on disconnect, as with PI-Desktop (#1966). `Clients()` gains it, `Detected()` does not, so the Agents page gains no row.

`UA` is the lower-case prefix that document asks for. `AgentOf` lower-cases the first word before matching, so `LobeHub/2.2.20` resolves to the same id.

The icon is LobeHub's own, the colour one from [lobe-icons](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-icons): `packages/static-svg/icons/lobehub-color.svg`, added as `internal/gui/assets/icons/lobehub-color.svg`. The `-color` name puts it through the image path rather than the mask path, so it keeps its colours as `codex-color.svg` does.

`internal/agent/lobehub_test.go`: the three spellings resolve to `lobehub`, and `Clients()` carries the entry with that name and icon. With the entry taken out it fails against unmodified `main` (`"LobeHub/2.2.20"` reads as `LobeHub`), so it is not a test that passes either way.

## Verified here

- `gofmt -l` on the changed files, `go vet -tags nogui ./...`, `go build -tags nogui ./...`: clean.
- `go test -tags nogui ./internal/agent ./internal/usage ./internal/usageapi`: pass.
- `go test -tags nogui ./internal/gateway`: `TestClaudeClientCacheAbsentUnchanged` fails, and fails the same way on unmodified `main` here, so not from this change.
- The icon renders at 128, 64, 32 and 18 px on light and dark backgrounds.

Not verified: the Routing page in a running magpie window. This machine has no gtk4/webkitgtk, so only `-tags nogui` was built; the icon is embedded in the binary and its path follows `staticFS()`, but I have not seen the row drawn.

## A question on the icon

At 18 px, the size the Routing page uses, LobeHub's logo reads as a silhouette but its details are gone — the artwork is detailed for a slot this small, and the icons already there are simpler shapes. Keep `lobehub-color.svg` as it is, or would a simplified mark serve better?
