items.title: gateway: image requests judge size by something other than the bytes held (draw.go has no per-image cap at all; holdWriter.wantWhole skips holdMost)
items.body:
**Written by an AI agent that read the code, not by a person using magpie.** I did not hit a crash myself; everything below is read from source at `dee5c9d7`/`75e769a9` and measured with `runtime.MemStats`. Flagging that up front so you can weigh it accordingly.

Two places in the image paths decide whether to hold something by a measure that isn't the memory it costs. The first one I fixed and pushed to my fork (link at the end); the second I did not touch.

## 1. `draw.go`: an image request has no per-image limit at all

`/v1/images/edits` reads its input images whole and never looks at what they cost. There is no byte cap, no pixel cap and no image-count cap on the way in.

- `readPart` (`internal/gateway/draw.go:768`) is an unbounded `io.ReadAll(f)` on each multipart part (`:774`).
- The JSON branch is an unbounded `io.ReadAll(r.Body)` (`draw.go:665`) followed by `json.Unmarshal` into `json.RawMessage` (`:681`), then `pictureOf` (`:749`) base64-decodes each `data:` URL (`:756`) with no size check.
- `d.Images` is appended to with no bound (`draw.go:651`, `:688`). `maxDrawings = 4` (`:82`, checked at `:710`) bounds **how many images are drawn**, not how many are sent in or fetched out.
- `draw.go` imports no `image/*`, so it cannot know an image's size even in principle: `rg -c 'image.DecodeConfig' internal/gateway/draw.go` → 0.

The only ceiling is the gateway-wide request body limit (`defaultBodyLimit`, 512 MB decoded, `request_bounds.go:28`). A single request can therefore hold the body, a second full copy (`draw.go:388` re-wraps `r.Body` over `inputBody` and `:665` reads it again), the raw-message copy, the decoded `picture.Data`, a freshly built data URL per image (`draw.go:355`), and the marshalled outgoing body. That is several multiples of 512 MB in one request, and `eachDrawing` (`draw.go:1450`) then runs up to `n` vendor requests at once, each holding its whole reply (capped at 256 MB by `draw.go:1036`).

Worth noting: `local(r)` (`lan.go:547`) lets a loopback request through without a gateway key, and `keyLimited` (`key_limit.go:36`) only bounds a key that has a limit set. So on a machine with magpie on it, an agent talking to `127.0.0.1` reaches this without any key.

## 2. `fallback.go`: `wantWhole` steps over the bound that exists

`holdWriter` holds a streamed reply only up to `holdMost` (1 MB, `fallback.go:1960`, checked at `:2086`). But `:2056` returns early when `wantWhole` is set, so a compaction summary's stream is held to its end with no byte bound at all.

`wantWhole` is deliberate for correctness (#2274 wants a summary whole or not at all), so the bound isn't wrong to skip it — the missing part is that nothing replaces it. A long history's summary is exactly where a reply is large, and it is held in full, per in-flight request.

## Why I think these are one report

Both are the same shape as the bug I did fix in `codex_images.go`: the guard existed but measured something other than the bytes actually held. Codex image fitting judged **pixels** (`80 << 20`) while the decoder allocates from the **declared header size times the format's bytes per pixel**, before it reads a single pixel. A 110-byte PNG declaring 8000x8000 at 16 bits a channel made `png.Decode` hold 488 MB, and four of them in one request held 1710 MB at `fitWorkers = 4` with no budget for what the four held between them. The decode then fails and the image goes as it came, so the bytes were spent for nothing.

## What I changed (for the codex path only)

Branch `gateway/codex-image-bytes` on my fork, one commit `84fe6317` on top of `75e769a9`:

- `codexImageMaxBytes = 320 << 20` replaces `codexImageMaxPixels`, and `imageHolds(cfg, format)` reads the bytes a decode will hold from the header alone (4 bytes a pixel for anything with colour or alpha, 1/2/8 as `image/png`'s `readImagePass` allocates, in `int64` so `70000x70000` can't wrap).
- `codexImageRefit` checks it before `png.Decode`/`jpeg.Decode`/`gif.Decode`, and also checks the base64 length before decoding it.
- `fitBudget = 512 << 20` batches what one request makes at once, so a request of 100 screenshots holds what 4 do.

320 MB is deliberately equal to the old `80<<20` pixels × 4 bytes, so nothing a real screenshot does changes: 3456x2234 holds 29 MB, 4032x3024 46 MB, 6000x4000 91 MB, all still fitted as before.

The new tests measure allocation (`runtime.MemStats` either side), because my first version only asserted that the image went as it came — and that passed on the old code, since the old decode also failed, just after spending the bytes. With the old behaviour put back: `TestCodexAHeaderAloneCantHoldPastTheBudget` fails with "110 bytes of upload held 488 MB" and `TestCodexFourHeadersInOneRequestCantHoldTheHeap` with "1299 bytes of upload, sent as 4 images in one request, held 1710 MB". Both pass with the change. `-race` passes, `go vet` on linux/windows passes, `gofmt` clean.

Full `go test -tags nogui ./...` fails in `internal/agent`, `internal/cli` and `internal/gateway` (`TestClaudeClientCacheAbsentUnchanged`); I reproduced each on clean `dee5c9d7` with my change stashed, so none is mine.

Fork branch: https://github.com/zzjcool/magpie/tree/gateway/codex-image-bytes

I'm not opening a PR unasked. If you want one for the codex part, say so and I'll open it against `main`; otherwise feel free to take the patch from the branch. The two items above I deliberately left alone — happy to do either as a separate change if you'd rather.

items.title: SenseNova turns Codex's structured-output requests away with guided_grammar compile_grammar_error — the refusal isn't recognized, the 400 reaches the client
items.body:
SenseNova's backend refuses Codex's structured-output requests (thread_title, thread_description) with a 400 its own words don't let magpie recognize, so the error reaches the client and every title and description a session asks of a SenseNova-served model fails.

## What happens

Codex sends its title and description turns with structured output — `text.format` carrying a json_schema. A model served by SenseNova compiles that schema in its guided decoder and turns the request away:

```json
{"error":{"code":"400","message":"sensenova: guided_grammar '{\"$schema\":\"https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema\",\"additionalProperties\":false,\"properties\":{\"description\":{\"minLength\":1,\"type\":\"string\"},\"title\":{\"maxLength\":36,\"minLength\":1,\"type\":\"string\"}},\"required\":[\"title\",\"description\"],\"type\":\"object\"}' has compile_grammar_error: No module named 'xgrammar'","param":null,"type":"invalid_request_error"}}
```

The backend is missing the `xgrammar` module its guided decoding needs. The same refusal comes from SenseNova's own API (`token.sensenova.cn`) and from a litellm relay in front of it.

## Why magpie doesn't adapt

SenseNova's docs allow `response_format {"type":"json_object"}` only — the JSON shape is prompted, not enforced — so magpie's built-in refusal cascade (`refusesFormat` → json_object with the schema in the instructions → words alone) fits exactly. But the refusal's words name no format field at all (`guided_grammar`, `compile_grammar_error`), none of which the refusal regex matches, so the cascade never runs. models.dev also marks `sensenova-6.8-flash-lite` as `structured_output: true`, which the backend's own behaviour contradicts.

## Reproduce

Any `/v1/responses` request carrying `text.format` json_schema to a SenseNova-served model (verified on `sensenova/sensenova-6.8-flash-lite` against `token.sensenova.cn`, 2026-10-20).

## Verified fix

A build with `guided_grammar` and `compile_grammar` added to the `formatRefusal` regex self-heals against the real backend: the refused schema is asked again as a `json_object` with the schema in the instructions (200), the form is remembered, and later requests run pre-adapted. Unpatched, the same request 400s every time.

The change is on my fork with a test whose fixture is the refusal word for word, and the routing reference's structured-output bullet brought up to date with the two-step cascade:

- branch: https://github.com/jasonQin6/magpie/tree/sensenova-guided-grammar-refusal (commit be83af2)

Opening a PR from that branch is refused for my account ("jasonQin6 does not have the correct permissions to execute CreatePullRequest" — the REST endpoint 404s too), so this issue is pointing at it instead. Fetching the branch or applying the patch from it works; happy to do either differently if there is a preferred way.

## Environment

magpie gateway on Linux (vol-server build), Codex 0.163 as the client, SenseNova over its Responses endpoint; a routing group of free SenseNova-channel models serves the aux tasks.

items.title: [feat] Claude subscription: a client opts in to place its own cache marks and TTLs (X-Magpie-Cache-Marks: client) (branch ready to merge)
items.body:
> **A branch ready to merge:** [`deephbz/magpie:feat/claude-client-cache-ttl`](https://github.com/deephbz/magpie/tree/feat/claude-client-cache-ttl), two commits on top of `main` at d9a050c: > > - [`90cdb2f`](https://github.com/deephbz/magpie/commit/90cdb2f41a7d9b313de7fee8ab68b13b61b1aae6): the opt-in. > - [`c4cf224`](https://github.com/deephbz/magpie/commit/c4cf2247bede5a6ae7ae30ae79dc8bb1e1c1a24a): usage keeps Anthropic's 5m/1h write split when no write is 1h. > > Both merge cleanly into `main` at 95e7c6b. The repository takes no pull requests, so they are offered here. [Compare with `main`](https://github.com/yetone/magpie/compare/main...deephbz:magpie:feat/claude-client-cache-ttl). > > ```sh > git fetch https://github.com/deephbz/magpie.git feat/claude-client-cache-ttl && git cherry-pick 90cdb2f c4cf224 > ``` ## Problem On the Anthropic Messages API, a client places up to four `cache_control` marks and gives each a TTL, `5m` or `1h`. magpie's Anthropic API-key provider forwards them unchanged. The Claude subscription bridge discards all of them: - `parseAnthropic` keeps no `cache_control`. - The run's first message puts the whole system prompt in one block. Two requests that share only the first part of their system prompt share no cache past Claude Code's own prompt. - Claude Code marks each request's end with its own TTL. A client can't choose between 5m and 1h. A client that needs a cache boundary at a given point, or a given TTL, gets neither through a subscription. ## Change A client opts in per request with the header `X-Magpie-Cache-Marks: client` on `/v1/messages` to a Claude subscription model. Without the header the bridge behaves as on `main`. Chat Completions and Responses ignore the header. ``` opted-in request ─▶ claude_cache.go: validate marks, count dropped ones └─▶ start run: DISABLE_PROMPT_CACHING=1 → all four slots are the client's ├─ system marks → end blocks of their own in the first message ├─ message marks → end blocks in a new run's rendered history ├─ top-level / last → {"cache_control":{…ttl}} in CLAUDE_CODE_EXTRA_BODY, │ set again before a turn that names another TTL └─ history-chunk mark → only in a free slot, never longer than an earlier mark ``` | Client mark | Bridge | Parity | | --- | --- | --- | | `cache_control` without `ttl` | 5m, as on the API | full | | System block | Ends its own block in the first message, same TTL | full | | Top-level `cache_control` | Request-level tail through `CLAUDE_CODE_EXTRA_BODY` | full | | Mark on the request's last block | Same tail | full | | Earlier message, new run | Ends a block at that message in the rendered history, same TTL | full | | Earlier message, running or saved run | Dropped and reported | gap | | Tool definition | Dropped and reported. Claude Code owns the tools. | gap | - **Validation, as on the API.** More than four marks, or a `1h` mark after a `5m` mark in tools → system → messages order, returns 400 with `type: error` and `invalid_request_error`. The count includes a top-level mark. Both messages match the live API's text. - **Report.** `X-Magpie-Cache-Marks-Dropped` lists dropped marks by section, for example `tools:1,messages:3`. It is absent when nothing was dropped. Only a Claude subscription try sets it. In a group, a try on another member, such as an Anthropic API key, keeps the marks and clears a report that an earlier Claude try left. On a streamed reply it is best-effort: a Claude subscription try waits at most 2 s for run selection before it sends headers. Other tries do not wait. - **Run identity.** The mode is part of the run key, including rewritten conversations and tool-result handoffs. Opted-in and ordinary requests never share a run. - **Usage** (`c4cf224`). `Usage.anthropic()` wrote `cache_creation` only when some writes were 1h. A request whose writes were all 5m lost the split in ordinary and streamed replies. Usage now records whether upstream reported the split and passes it on, even at 0/0. Only a nonzero write count replaces an earlier one, so a later update that reports 0/0 keeps the earlier writes. When a reply's usage is summed over earlier tries, search rounds or internal messages, an update adds the earlier writes only if its own total is nonzero. If the update's split has counts (5m + 1h > 0) but no 1h writes, it first keeps the current message's known 1h count; then it adds the earlier messages' usage. A zero-filled or absent split keeps `main`'s rule for each counter. A zero-filled split with a nonzero total is not passed on to the client. It invents no split for usage that reported none. This also applies without the header. - [`claude-subscription-bridge.md`](docs/subsystems/claude-subscription-bridge.md) has a new "Client-placed cache marks" section with the table, the gaps and the test command. **Limit.** A request that branches from an earlier turn of a running run's conversation, with a new ask added, starts a new run. That run is told the conversation in one rendered message. Its prefix can't match the turns the running run cached, so it reads only the shared prefix. On the API the same request reads the whole earlier prompt. Cache reuse for such requests needs another mechanism. This branch does not try one. ## Evidence
Live at 0c9298d: usage after the first summing fix (not rerun at c4cf224) `claude-haiku-5-5`, the same setup as below, gateway built from `0c9298d`, baseline from d9a050c. | Case | Result | | --- | --- | | Opted in, mark without `ttl`, ordinary and streamed | Write 3,843, split 3,843/0, as upstream sent. Streamed `message_start` and `message_delta` both carry it. | | Tail 5m → 1h → 5m in one running run | One launch. Read/write 0/5,580 (1,727/3,853), 3,853/1,944 (0/1,944), 5,797/40 (40/0), as upstream sent. | | No header, through the Claude subscription, cold then warm | 0/5,577, then 5,577/0, as upstream sent. | | No header, through the `anthropic` API-key provider, cold then warm | 0/3,747, then 3,747/0, as upstream sent. | | No header, request with `ttl` marks | The request magpie sent to Anthropic equals the baseline's. | Your probe (earlier writes 30, `message_start` 20, then a 0/0 split) gives 50. The no-split row from the reply below gives 60 with 35 of it 1h.
Live at 90cdb2f + bb9b965: groups, fallback, usage and the opt-out `claude-haiku-5-5` through Claude Code on a Claude subscription and through magpie's `anthropic` provider on an API key, via a dev gateway built from `bb9b965`, with a recording proxy in front of Anthropic. A gateway built from d9a050c ran beside it as the baseline. Read and write are cache tokens; the split is 5m/1h writes. | Case | Result | | --- | --- | | Group [API key, Claude], opted in, one tool mark; ordinary and streamed | The API-key member answers. No `X-Magpie-Cache-Marks-Dropped`. Upstream receives `tools[0].cache_control`. | | Group [Claude, API key], the same request | Claude answers and reports `tools:1`. | | The Claude try fails to launch, the API-key member answers; ordinary and streamed | No report from the failed Claude try. | | API-key reply delayed 17 s | First keepalive at 15.88 s in the group and at 15.03 s on the API key directly. No 2 s hold. | | Tail 5m → 1h → 5m in one running run | One launch. Read/write 0/5,580 (split 1,727/3,853), 3,853/1,866 (0/1,866), 5,719/40 (40/0). | | Mark without `ttl`, ordinary and streamed | 5m on the wire. Write 3,842, split 3,842/0, in `message_start` and `message_delta`. | | Tool mark; message mark on a running run | `tools:1`, then `tools:1,messages:1` in the same run. | | No header, request with `ttl` marks | The request magpie sent to Anthropic equals the baseline's. Warmed read/write 5,571/0 on both. | Your zero-write probe (`message_start` 30 writes, then a `message_delta` with 0/0) gives `CacheWrite=30` at both commits, and `bb9b965` returns the split as 30/0.
Live at the first version (f3d138d, on v0.1.1220): each case through the bridge Claude Code 2.1.296 (`claude-haiku-5-5`) on a Claude subscription, through a dev gateway built from `f3d138d`, with a recording proxy in front of Anthropic. A `v0.1.1220` gateway ran beside it as the baseline. Read and write are cache tokens; the split is 5m/1h writes. | Case | Result | | --- | --- | | System marks, two new runs that share the first system block | Both 1h boundaries kept. Read/write 1,942/2,214, then 3,815/341. | | Tail 5m → 1h → 5m in one running run | One launch. Read/write 2,224/3,356 (split 1,727/1,629), 3,853/1,953 (0/1,953), 5,806/40 (40/0). | | Mark without `ttl` | 5m on the wire. Write 1,894, split 1,894/0. | | Message mark, two new runs of 20 and 40 messages | Client 1h boundary kept; the history-chunk mark takes a free slot. Read/write 1,942/6,011, then 7,953/5,728. | | Tool mark; message mark on a running run | `tools:1`, then `tools:1,messages:1`. The second request stays in its run: 4,553/403. | | Five marks; 1h after 5m | 400 before any run starts, with the API's shape and text. | | No header, request with `ttl` marks (5m system, 1h message, 5m top-level) | The request magpie sent to Anthropic, marks included, equals the baseline's. Warmed read/write 5,581/0 on both. | | Opted in, out, in again | Three runs. Opted-in runs carry the client's marks; the ordinary run carries Claude Code's four 1h marks. | | A real client that places marks and switches its tail TTL at runtime | Writes 5m → 1h → 5m as asked. Final turn read/write 18,895/408, split 408/0, same as upstream. | Streamed replies carry the 5m split in both `message_start` and `message_delta`. Branched request from an earlier turn: the bridge read 4,613 of a 20,137-token earlier prompt. Through the Anthropic API-key provider the same shape read 17,022 of 17,026.
Reference: the Anthropic API-key provider Same marks through magpie's `anthropic` provider on an API key, `claude-haiku-5-5`: | Request | Read | Write | | --- | --- | --- | | System 1h, message 1h, top-level mark without `ttl` | 0 | 10,463 (5m 2,835, 1h 7,628) | | The same again | 10,463 | 0 | | 1h mark after a 5m mark | 400: `a ttl='1h' cache_control block must not come after a ttl='5m' cache_control block…` | | | Six marks | 400: `A maximum of 4 blocks with cache_control may be provided. Found 6.` | |
## Tests New in `claude_client_cache_test.go`: - `TestClaudeClientCachePrompt`, `TestClaudeClientCacheHistorySlot`: system and message boundaries, default TTL, the history-chunk mark in a free slot. - `TestClaudeClientCacheValidation`, `TestClaudeClientCacheServerValidationBeforeStreaming`: both 400s, before any stream starts. - `TestClaudeClientCacheRunningTailAndDrops`, `TestClaudeClientCachePrefixRestart`: tail update and clear, drops on a running run, a tail that the kept marks can't take. - `TestClaudeClientCacheAbsentUnchanged`: without the header, the run's environment, prompt and report are unchanged. - `TestClaudeClientCacheIdentity`: opted-in and ordinary requests get different run keys, and the identity step adds no bytes to an ordinary key. It holds no stored hash, so other changes to the key don't break it. - `TestClaudeClientCacheGroupKeyKeepsMarks`, `TestClaudeClientCacheTryKeepalive`: in a group, in both orders and both stream modes, only a Claude subscription try reports drops or holds keepalives. - `TestClaudeClientCacheOtherAPIsIgnoreHeader`: Chat and Responses ignore the header. - `TestClaudeClientCacheUsage`, `TestClaudeClientCacheStreamingHeaders`: usage split; the report's hold, timeout and release. New in `usage_cache_split_test.go`: `TestAnthropicCacheSplitPresence`, `TestAnthropicCacheSplitUpdatesAndTotals`, `TestAnthropicCacheSplitZeroDeltaKeepsWrites`, `TestAnthropicCacheSplitZeroDeltaKeepsEarlierRound`, `TestAnthropicCacheSplitUnreportedDeltaKeepsHour`, `TestOtherUsageDoesNotInventAnthropicSplit`. New in `usage_cache_partial_test.go`: `TestCachePartialUpdateMatrix` runs 12 split cases through the bridge, a cut and retried stream, and search (streamed and not), and expects `main`'s totals and 1h counts. `TestCacheZeroFilledPartialUpdateOmitsSplit`: no invented 50/0 split. New in `usage_cache_zero_split_test.go`: your zero-filled probe in the bridge, continuation and search shapes (`TestProbe1717BridgeTotalZeroSplit`, `TestProbe1717ContinuationTotalZeroSplit`, `TestProbe1717SearchTotalZeroSplit`). New in `usage_cache_rounds_test.go`: `TestStreamCutZeroCacheSplitKeepsWrites` (a cut try retried), `TestClaudeInternalMessagesKeepCacheWrites` (the bridge's internal messages). New in `search_test.go`: `TestSearchZeroCacheSplitKeepsWrites`. Each sends 30 writes, then 20, then a 0/0 split, and expects 50.
Failures with parts of the change taken out Each guarantee was broken by hand once; each time a behavior test failed, not the build. - `90cdb2f`, 25 cases: default TTL, system and message boundaries, top-level and last-block tails, running and tool drops, history slot and TTL order, both validations, `DISABLE_PROMPT_CACHING`, run identity, report present and absent, tail update and clear, opt-in scope, other APIs, kept prefix TTL, streaming hold, timeout and release, usage TTLs. - The usage commit, 10 cases: split presence in both parsers, serialization at 0 h, merge of updates, full and sparse sums, no split from other protocols. - 9 more for the group report and the zero update: every try reporting, an earlier try's report or hold left in place, a hold on an API-key try, no hold on a Claude try, ordinary identity bytes written, a reported zero replacing total or 1h writes, split presence lost. Without the group fix, `TestClaudeClientCacheGroupKeyKeepsMarks` fails with `API-key reply reports dropped marks: "tools:1"` in both orders and both stream modes. Without the zero rule, `TestAnthropicCacheSplitZeroDeltaKeepsWrites` fails with `zero delta erased cache writes: got 0, want 30`. For the summing rule, these variants: | Variant | Failure | | --- | --- | | `bb9b965`'s rule (split presence allows the sum) | The usage, retried-stream, search and bridge tests give 30, want 50 | | Both counters gated on the update's total | The no-split row gives 60/20, want 60/35 | | `main`'s rule (each counter on its own value) | A pure-5m update after a 1h message gives split 50/0, want 30/20 | | `0c9298d`'s rule (a nonzero total carries the whole split) | Your zero-filled probe gives 1h 10, want 15, in the bridge, continuation and search | | Split counts carry the earlier 1h without the current message's 1h | A 5m-only or partial split after a `message_start` with 1h 5 gives 50/10, want 50/15 | | Each of the three callers skipping the new step | That caller's matrix cases give 50/10 | | The zero-filled split passed on | The client gets an invented 50/0 split | Without the split-presence change: ``` --- FAIL: TestClaudeClientCacheUsage/pure5m/stream_false claude_client_cache_test.go:405: missing "cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":1894,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":0} from {…"cache_creation_input_tokens":1894}} --- FAIL: TestClaudeClientCacheUsage/pure5m/stream_true claude_client_cache_test.go:405: missing "cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":1894,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":0} from event: message_start --- FAIL: TestClaudeClientCacheUsage/reportedZero/stream_false --- FAIL: TestClaudeClientCacheUsage/reportedZero/stream_true ```
Acceptance checks at c4cf224 Run under a temporary HOME with `GOPATH`, `GOMODCACHE` and `GOCACHE` pinned. | Check | Result | | --- | --- | | `gofmt -l` on changed files; `git diff --check` | nothing printed | | `go vet -tags nogui ./...` · `GOOS=linux` and `GOOS=windows go vet -tags nogui ./internal/gateway/` | pass | | `go test -tags nogui ./internal/gateway/ -count=1` | pass (296 s) | | `go test -race -tags nogui ./internal/gateway/ -run 'Test.*(Cache\|Usage\|Continuation\|StreamCut\|Search\|Claude\|Resume)\|TestProbe1717'` | pass (75 s) | | Cherry-pick of both commits onto `main` at 95e7c6b, then the focused tests with `-race` | clean, pass |
**Not run:** the full repository test suite (only `./internal/gateway/`), GUI tests (no GUI change), and a check on Linux or Windows hardware.
Original issue text (superseded) > **A branch ready to merge:** [`deephbz/magpie:feat/claude-client-cache-marks`](https://github.com/deephbz/magpie/tree/feat/claude-client-cache-marks), one commit, [`c233dc6`](https://github.com/deephbz/magpie/commit/c233dc651b46f164ac0b9c3e79236476a6864900), on top of the branch of #1716 ([`7ebe5a9`](https://github.com/deephbz/magpie/commit/7ebe5a957864c77bd0238195e25a96d3e9c57749)), which is on `main` at 6c1c0a7. Both merge cleanly. The repository takes no pull requests, so it is offered here. [Compare with `main`](https://github.com/yetone/magpie/compare/main...deephbz:magpie:feat/claude-client-cache-marks). > > ```sh > git fetch https://github.com/deephbz/magpie.git feat/claude-client-cache-marks && git cherry-pick 7ebe5a9 c233dc6 > ``` ## Problem A client can place Anthropic's cache marks itself, with a TTL on each. A Pi extension can do this, for example: - **G**: a 1h mark after the global system prompt, before the project's part. Every project shares the global part. - **P**: a 1h mark at the end of the system prompt. - **Tail**: a mark on the conversation's end. The user picks 5m or 1h at runtime. - **Fork**: a background compaction request is the conversation as it stood at a turn A, with its own ask added. It is sent while the conversation goes on, and it should read the cache the main request wrote at A. The Anthropic API-key path already forwards these marks unchanged. The Claude subscription bridge drops all of them: - `parseAnthropic` keeps no `cache_control` in the IR. - The run's first message puts the whole system prompt in one block. A second project shares nothing past Claude Code's own prompt. - Claude Code marks the request's end with its own TTL, so the client's 5m/1h choice has no effect. - A compaction request at an earlier turn matches no waiting run. A new run is told the whole conversation in one message and writes all of it to the cache again. ## Change A client that names a TTL (`5m` or `1h`) on its marks places them itself (`claude_cache.go`). Marks that name no TTL leave the run as before. Claude Code on an API key and Pi's default send unnamed marks, and honoring them would turn Claude Code's 1h marks into 5m ones. ``` client marks ─▶ parseAnthropic (Part.Cache, Request.SystemCache, CacheTail) └─▶ startRun: DISABLE_PROMPT_CACHING=1 → all four marks are the client's ├─ G, P → end blocks of their own in the first message (instructionMarks) ├─ tail → {"cache_control":{…ttl}} in CLAUDE_CODE_EXTRA_BODY (setSafeguards), │ sent again when a request names another TTL; never longer than an earlier mark ├─ history chunk mark (#1716) → in the room that is left └─ fork (claude_fork.go): --resume --fork-session --resume-session-at ``` - **Request-level tail.** Claude Code builds the request, so the bridge can't mark the last block itself. Claude Code passes a top-level `cache_control` from `CLAUDE_CODE_EXTRA_BODY` to Anthropic, which applies it to the last block of each request. `setSafeguards` already sets `EXTRA_BODY` per turn with `apply_flag_settings`. It now adds the tail. Anthropic refuses a 1h mark after a 5m one, so the tail is never longer than the shortest kept mark (`floor`). - **Fork from the run's session.** A run records, for each request it answers, the request's `turnKey` and its reply's message `uuid` (from the stream's `assistant` envelope). A later request whose messages, minus what it adds, match a recorded point starts Claude Code with `--resume --fork-session --resume-session-at `. The fork's request then repeats the run's request up to A and reads it from the cache. The new run gets only what the request adds. - Claude Code joins a new user message to the user message before it, and adds `"\n"` to that message's text. A fork resumed after a text turn would change the run's prefix. So after a text turn the fork starts before that turn and is told the turn again, then the request's additions. After tool results it starts at them. - `CLAUDE_CODE_TOTAL_TOKENS_REMINDER=off` (in `cleanClaudeEnv`). Claude Code adds a `…` block after each user turn, and that block split the run's prefix from the fork's. It also reports Claude Code's own budget, not the client's. - `turnKey` and `looseTurn` hold `clientCaches()`. A run with client marks never takes a turn without them, nor the other way. - [`claude-subscription-bridge.md`](docs/subsystems/claude-subscription-bridge.md) has a new "Client-placed cache marks" section and lists the new tests. ## Evidence
Claude Code behaviour this relies on (2.1.296, direct probes) - Five marks in one request → 400 ("maximum of 4 blocks"). Claude Code's own caching uses three. - With `DISABLE_PROMPT_CACHING=1`, Claude Code places no marks. Marks in the content it is told pass through. - `CLAUDE_CODE_EXTRA_BODY={"cache_control":{"type":"ephemeral","ttl":…}}` puts a request-level mark on each request, and it moves with the conversation. An `apply_flag_settings` change between turns took effect: the writes went 5m → 1h → 5m. - `--resume --fork-session --resume-session-at ` keeps the session up to and including the named entry. The `uuid` on the stream's `assistant` envelope is the session file's entry `uuid`. That envelope arrives before `content_block_stop`.
Live: each case through the bridge Claude Code 2.1.296 (`claude-haiku-5-5`) on a Claude subscription, through a dev gateway, with a recording proxy in front of Anthropic. Each request had a global part (G) and a project part (P). Claude Code's prompt and G came to about 20k tokens, and P to about 5k. The runs used a build of this commit before a rename and wording-only edit (`setExtraBody` → `setSafeguards`, comments). The tests below cover the final commit. | Case | Request | Cache read | Cache write | |---|---|---|---| | **G shared** | project X, new | 0 | 1h 25,960 | | | project Y, new, same global part | 20,384 | 1h 5,175 | | **Tail TTL per request** | turn 1, tail 5m | 0 | 5m 1,459 (+1h 25,960 for G, P) | | | turn 2, tail 1h | 25,960 | 1h 2,807 | | | turn 3, tail 5m | 28,767 | 5m 1,183 | | **Fork after a text turn** | M2 (turn A) | 32,219 | 5m 5,270 | | | M3 (main goes on) | 37,489 | 5m 88 | | | fork at A + handoff | 37,489 | 5m 18 | | **Fork after tool results** | M2 (turn A, tool result) | 32,252 | 5m 5,204 | | | M3 (main goes on) | 37,456 | 5m 161 | | | fork at A + handoff | 37,456 | 5m 24 | Every request had at most four marks. The gateway log showed `starts from that run's session` for both forks. An earlier version resumed the fork after A's own user message. That fork read only 32,265 and wrote 5,320, because of the `"\n"` join and the token countdown block. The fork design above is the fix for that.
## Tests - **`TestClaudeClientCacheMarksKept`** (new, `claude_client_cache_test.go`): G and P end blocks of their own, and another project's first block is the same. The history mark takes the room that is left. A 5m system prompt makes the history mark and tail 5m. No more than four marks are kept. Unnamed marks render as before. - **`TestClaudeClientCacheRun`** (new): a run with client marks starts with `DISABLE_PROMPT_CACHING=1` and `EXTRA_BODY` tail 5m. The next turn in the same run switches it to 1h. A request without named marks gets Claude Code's own caching and no `EXTRA_BODY` change. - **`TestClaudeForkStartsFromTheRunsSession`** (new): a compaction request at turn 2 of a run on turn 3 starts `--resume --fork-session --resume-session-at `. It is told turn 2 and the ask, nothing earlier. The main conversation goes on in its run. A request at the run's first turn, or one no run answered, starts anew. - The test harness of `claude_resume_test.go` gets `newTurnHarness`, so a test can add lines to its stand-in Claude Code's turn. It also logs control requests.
Failures with parts of the change taken out Without the production code the new tests don't compile. With one part broken at a time: ``` ## fork hook removed (start never calls fork) --- FAIL: TestClaudeForkStartsFromTheRunsSession claude_client_cache_test.go:200: the fork: ## clientCaches always false --- FAIL: TestClaudeClientCacheMarksKept claude_client_cache_test.go:66: client caches false, tail "5m", floor "1h" --- FAIL: TestClaudeClientCacheRun claude_client_cache_test.go:167: first run: ## tail fixed at 5m (the request's TTL ignored) --- FAIL: TestClaudeClientCacheRun claude_client_cache_test.go:171: the next turn, its end for an hour: ## fork resumed after the text turn --- FAIL: TestClaudeForkStartsFromTheRunsSession claude_client_cache_test.go:200: the fork: ```
Acceptance checks at c233dc6 Run under a temporary HOME with `GOPATH`, `GOMODCACHE` and `GOCACHE` pinned and `XDG_*` unset. | Check | Result | |---|---| | `gofmt -l` on changed files | nothing printed | | `go vet -tags nogui ./...` · `GOOS=linux go vet -tags nogui ./...` · `GOOS=windows go vet ./internal/gateway/` | pass | | `GOOS=linux go build -tags nogui` · `GOOS=windows go build` | pass | | `CGO_ENABLED=0 go test -tags nogui ./...` | 49 packages pass | | `go test -race -tags nogui ./internal/gateway/ -run 'ClaudeClientCache\|ClaudeForkStarts\|AutoMode\|Safeguard\|ClaudeEndedRun'` | pass | | The three new tests, `-count=100` | pass |
**Not run:** a Pi session end to end with a cache-marking extension and a real background compaction. The live probe sent requests of the same shape to the gateway. Also not run: GUI tests (no GUI change), and a check on Linux or Windows hardware. **Limits:** a fork is found only while the run that answered turn A is live and keeps that point (the last 64 per run). A fork from a run started anew at its first turn starts anew, because that first message is magpie's rendering, which no fork repeats.
